So I have the Chinese and Spanish.
For The game in general, The way it work is that you are in an apartment you get to explore. You  the ability to switch between third person and first person, and the bases of the game is that you click on objects, the game pronounces the word, the transation and shows the word. you then have the choice to add the word to your vocab list. This applies for nouns and verbs with the verbs being attached to an object that is related to the verb ( for example, the verb "To watch" is attached to the Television). for every ten words you select to add, a new list consisting of just those words in made, and then you are able to test yourself on the list. the test works  be you get the option to isolate how much of the word you get in order find the object (For example, you can choice to have just the word appear with no voice or clues to the direction of the object, or you can just pick to hear the voice and no text to aid you).
You progress in the game by testing youself on these words you obtain, and then successfully picking any word three times in a row. once you do that, you receive a gold star ( which is used to buy verbs and adjectives off of objects) and the word is considered mastered. you beat the game by mastering all the words of all the objects in the apartment.
For any langauge, this game is a perfect way to improve your ear for the langauge and to better introduce yourself with more vocabulary.
now to the langauges
The Chinese is nice, it has a selection to do pinyin and later characters. The tones for each word is clear, the speaker is very good at what it's doing. The problem is that you often will recieve a word with synonyms, which happens in each language, but with Mandarin chinese being so regional, the game doesn't explain which words are used where (Such as tailand or main land china.)
Spanish is great, the pronounciations are clear, with the speaker leaning towards a latin american accent. the langauge is standard, with the words you receive being the most understood word, with synonyms being out shined by this standard words. again, a problem is that the game doesnt explain which words are used where, but I guess you can google it or something.
not much more to say,
Not a good game to learn a langauge's grammer,
a great game for people with an understanding of a language's grammer that want to expand thier vocab.

Functionally equivalent to flash cards. Lacking some basic usability features, interface can be a little cumbersome and doesn't control well in first person. Word mastery feels arbitrary. Vocab limited to your 4-room apartment as well so some of the words are a little specialist. Reverse translation would be very helpful but is conspicuously absent. Plenty of room for this game to improve but will probably never be more than a fun supplement to learning a new language. You will get out of it as much as you put in, just as with any language tool.

Influent is the best 'gamification' of vocabulary learning I have come across. I have spent over 10 hours with the Russian edition, I hesitate to call it a game so I'll say "application". Reading the negative reviews I am dissapointed with the community. You are simply a fool if you think you can just 'play' this and somehow become fluent or even remotely competent in your chosen language. Even a basic level of comprehension takes at least a year to develop with a lot of hard work involved in that year.
Influent will not teach grammar, it is simply and audio/visual application that softens the monumentual blow of learning hundreds of foreign words. Personally I have found it incredibly useful.
It works by giving you control of an avatar in a typical apartment, you can swap between third and first person to explore and click on items to have a native speaker exclaim what the items is and you're also given a textual display of the item. You can then choose to add the item to a vocab list and once you add 10 items it completes the list and allows you to come back at any point to attempt a 'Time Attack' where the items in the list are randomised, the native speaker announces what item they want you to find.
I highly recommend Influent as an AID to your language learning, not the only source.

Endless Legend has a really good start, but a disappointing ending. At the beginning, it proves itself apart and against its predecessors with gusto; a nice video intro, interactive tutorial, unique factions each with their own advantages/disadvantages and (wow!) individual main questlines (there seems to be one without its own questline for now, but I expect that would be fixed in the future). The world is well-varied and well-organized into regions so as to retain a large feel without getting cumbersome and overwhelming. The seasons change and with it, everything from resource gain to army movements. Gameplay has been smooth and early on, rich and rewarding. There's a lot to love, and I do love it.
But at a certain point, it turns into a grind, and continues to grind until we're glad to see it all end. I'd say it starts about... 60% of the way through the game. This is when all the ruins are explored, and all the territories are colonized, and all the empires are jostling each other and would either start warring or everyone just sits still doing nothing much. Meanwhile questlines keep talking about how things are getting worse, as if there was a sense of urgency, but we never see that happen on the main map. In fact, we only see our cities getting more and more prosperous, and no cause for any urgency or concern of any kind (unless we'd been idiots early on and got ourselves into more wars than we can manage).
I, for one, would dearly love to see that 'end of the world is coming' feasibly manifested on the main map. Something like Sid Meiers Alpha Centauri spawning stronger and stronger aliens might be nice. Or otherwise some sort of added dimension of discovery during mid-late game, like a subterranean layer or sea colonies (an orbital layer happened before, but this isn't the kind of game to allow that... probably).
Most of all, I'd love to see a proper ending, something more than just a unit moving differently (Vaulters) than normal. A closing video would be nice.

Endless Legend is a surprisingly good 4X game, it outclasses Civ4 and Civ5 for me. There's something really enthralling about micromanaging my empire, I feel the "just one more turn" aspect of the game should almost be illegal. A large part of my enjoyment I think is the ability to auto-resolve battles (the AI takes care of both players moves, and the battle is determined in a second) leaves more time to do the stuff I like most about these games, get the research going, manage the population, laugh at the mind-boggling moves the AI sometimes makes. These aspects of the game are fantastic.
Multiplayer is pretty swanky too, although I enjoy single-player more as the few multiplayer games I've played the player who understands the combat the best (i.e., what equipment is best, and actually pays attention to unit composition of their army) steamrolls the other players. This isn't a bad thing, it just means I need to git gud :P

I'm going to try to keep this short.
Endless Legend is, without a doubt, the best turn-based 4x fantasy game on the market. It even beats out, IMO, non-fantasy games like Civ 5.
The primary reason for this is that unlike Civ 5, each faction in this game is totally unique. With all the DLC that's 10 completely unique factions (8 in the base game) with their own personailty, unique units, buildings and lore. They do not play alike. I'm not talking about a minor bonus or malus to a random attribute. I mean that there are races that cannot declare war. races that can only be at war, races that can only have a single city and races who use what seems like magic.
The developers are phenominal in the way they interact with the community and make additions and changes based on feedback. In fact, the major work that the AI has recently received is largely based on that feedback and makes the game truly shine above any competition.
There are no downsides to getting this game that I can name apart from the horrible one-more-turn addiction.

This is a kart racing game that while not as good as the Nintendo ones, it's still pretty good. It plays as you'd expect, with a drifting mechanic that rewards with boosting and with items that you can use against your opponents. There's 20 racers (8 from the Sonic universe) with enough differences between them, some more noticeable than others. There's 8 locations (3 from the Sonic universe) with 3 tracks each, totaling 24. The tracks are colorful and designed for drifting and boosting, although some are trickier than others. The soundtrack is ripped from the original games, but i only found it okay. The commentator is kind of annoying, but you can turn it off. However, there isn't much content here. The gran prix is just 6 series of 4 races in all of the 24 circuits. Mission mode is the most interesting one, featuring a mix of racing, battles, drifting challenges, and other things. Time trial is just that, driving through the stages to beat your best time. And there's some in-game achievements. The game is also easy, and i recommend you to play on expert. The steam version however lacks achievements, leaderboards, steam cloud, multiplayer (there's only split-screen) and trading cards. The game is good, don't get me wrong, but today it feels like it's a big prologue for it's much improved sequel, Sonic & All-Stars Racing Transformed. It's like a preparation for that game. For cheap, i can recommend it, but don't expect much depth like it's sequel.

It had very fun puzzle mechanics later on in the game where you would travel between the 8-bit world and the fully developed 3D world in order to progress and it made gameplay very interesting.  The storyline is more of a tool than an actual story since gameplay and the story closely mirror FF7/Zelda but it is humorous at times.  Gameplay was pretty cool in that it featured all sorts of gameplay including a very sillly Diablo level featuring tons of gear for example a ring of item finding which had a description of "helps you find an actually useful item".
The bad parts I would say are the RPG gameplay sections which I feel don't develop enough, and the very short length of the game.
Overall, it was a very fun game and I would buy it if it went on sale again if I were you.  You can really tell the developer put a lot of love into the game.

My first strategy-type game I have ever played in my childhood. This is where my thirst and hunger for winning started. This may not be for people that are playing a game and evaluating it from a graphical side. It is 2002 game, so.. In my opinion it is pretty strategic and fun to play.
My first time that I had to play this game was horrible, because I had absolutelly no logic (Yes, you need to have brain to play this game. This is not just building and done). What I was doing back then just building beautiful buildings, such as church and etc. I didn't know what I was doing. So, when I grew up, I got into this game out of nostalgia. I understood what I was doing at that time, and it was lmao to remember what I was doing back there... xD
So, as I said, this game needs logic, because you are not going to survive and win by doing random♥♥♥♥♥♥ You start up in different locations of the map with your opponents and you the point is to build your castle, make troops and protect yourself and slaughter them. But the most logical part of the game, is management of resources. Gold, stone, wood, food, iron. Nothing complicated. The food is the most essential resource for surviving obviously. Without it, people will leave your castle and you have nothing... So after you have dispatched resource income in appriopriate way and value, you have to build up you castle (That's my favourite part, because you can build in any way you want) and protect it, because everything is risky. They can target your resource income building, which can leave you empty and put you at a disadvantage. Thinking through stuff, and protecting everything is the key. After building up stage, some obviously will choose to attack, and some of them will have to defend. Defending is the most fun part, because after you dispatched your troops at appropriate locatons of defense (such as towers) for protection, it is so satisfying to see how strong is your defense, and after that you can find your weakness. Then, it is up to you, you build up your army, you slaughter, you win. That's all.
Also there are campaign and other modes which can give a little bit of a challenge against other opponents. Some stages will be hard, and will give you a location with disadvantages, but it is up to you how you will build up, survive, destroy and win.
That I think is everything to this game. I recommend it for players that are interested in strategic. (Bu I am guessing there are people who have started their journey from this one and what I mean is that they already tried it).

I couldn't really decide between 3 and 4, so i give it a 3,5. This game can be good to play sometimes, and can be boring sometimes. In this game, you have to box with bears, which is a nice entertainment factor, instead of those silly bandits in most of these fighting games. At the beginning it's really fun to play. But when you get into the later stages of the game, you find yourself repetitively pressing the same buttons against the same enemies. In this game, there are 2 kinds of enemies, a slim bear/fox mixture, and a real big bear. Every level consists of 3-4 waves of enemies, and then a big boss (the real big bear). Every single level is the same, but the enemies wear different clothes and the background changes. The game tries to hide it (and it does the hiding very well) , but it feels repetitive. I completed this game just by smashing the S button all the way :) But there are some interesting things in the gameplay, for example the skill system. You can level up in this game after every stage, and, i couldn't really get it how it works, you just go and level up. Without experience gaining to track your progress, This makes leveling pretty unpredictable. Sometimes you gain 2 levels, sometimes 1. Pretty random thing. But, when you level up you can choose which skill you want to improve. Every level up you gain 1 point which you can spend on increasing your Health, Power, Speed, and the Special Skill. I liked this part of the game.

OHHH MY GOD! This game is so funny! I actually completed this game because of the high amount of sense of humor this game has. The creators must be comedians, or i don't know, but i was falling out of the chair all the time because of those jokes. For example the strip bar in the game, which is called "Bare Bears", and un-bear-able, and these silly jokes. I laughed my *ss off literally. This game is only good because of its humor, in my opinion. As i've said earlier, this is not my genre, but who wouldn't want to laugh?

Audio isn't that bad either. The sound effects are good, there are some funny ones like the one at the jumping kicks (WOHOOOOOO or something like that), and the normal punch and kick sound effects. The Backgrounds musics are well done, i haven't got any problems with them. They always fitted the scene.

The plot is pretty dumb, but easy to understand and good! :)
The game starts with the protagonist's (Tim Burr) celebration, and then some noise comes and the screen flashes, and everything turns bad, his house is on fire, the forest is burning. Then suddenly from the middle of the nowhere, Tim Burr's hand(just one hand) changes into the Fist of Awesome, and it begins to talk to him, surprising Tim. Then they beat up lots of enemies, and so on, and they travel in time with Lorentzian Traversable Wormholes. They go back to Dinosaurs, to Medieval ages and other places. It's pretty interesting. The game even tricks us, when we destroy the time travel machine(near the end), the time travels back to the celebration, where we think that finally the game is over, The leader of the bears (The Fist of Awesome's brother) repairs the time machine and everything goes wrong again. And then we have to struggle 2 more levels to complete the game, at the end killing the Fist of Awesome's brother. And then, finally we get back to the celebration, where we find ourselves that this celebration is a marriage, and everyone congratulates our actions. And then at the very end, we have to choose who to marry, a stinky lumberjack or a girl, sadly, i didn't read the last texts just ran to the lumberjack and he kissed me, well, i was surprised a little bit.
In summary, i liked it, it was fun.

I've an affinity for many of the Lego Games, most especially the Lego Marvel Superheroes game, which happened to have the best combination of open world with smooth controls, hilarious dialogue, and just looked sweet!
Batman 3 Beyond Gotham iterates on the system. I've played/own a ton of Lego games, and I gotta say that with Batman 3, it's really apparent how TT's matured much of their control scheming and gameplay "modes". Comparitvely, flying is a lot smoother than it was in Batman 2, and I think they've taken a lot of the critical feedback to heart and really optimized the game well. I haven't had many frame stutters, and I'm running max settings all around.
I really appreciate the suit changing system too, which in Batman 2 involved you finding a suit changing station. That was pretty tedious to say the least, but Batman 3 makes it much more fun by allowing players to switch to the various suits at any time simply by holding a button down (Y, if you use an X360 controller).
I haven't spotted any errors/glitches, and I haven't touched Open World yet, but if it's anything like it was in the Marvel game, it's gonna be awesome. Really, I'm only a few hours in, but already I can see myself repeating my gameplay for a long time! Looking forward to seeing TT fold these new iterations into the next Marvel Superheroes 2!

Ryse: Son of Rome is an action videogame developed by Crytek that revolves around a skilled officer of the ancient Roman Empire army, Marius Titus, who, after being involved in the disastrous Roman campaign in Britannia, embarks in a quest for revenge back in the capital.
The bread and butter of Ryse is moving Marius through the various levels and cut down the many enemies he has to face in the quickest and most efficent way possible. In order to do so, you are given different moves (both to attack and defend yourself) and chains of QTEs finishers to dispatch weakened foes. When it comes to combat, the game gets progressively more challenging, with later enemies requiring specific strategies in order to be killed (for instance, shielded enemies need to be briefly stunned before attacking and dual wielding enemies are open to be attacked only after a series of successful parries). Marius also has a focus gauge that he can use to activate a super mode of some sort and killing enemies award you valor, which can be used to buy upgrades for the protagonist. The average sword fighting gameplay is only briefly interrupted by some sequences that require you to use ranged weapons against enemies or other obstacles or command an entire Roman legion towards a certain location (which mainly boils down to move forward, shield yourself from enemy arrows and shoot back once in a while). This, coupled with the few bosses not offering any sudden and imaginative gameplay change and the main campaign being somehow brief (around five or six hourse), make Ryse: Son of Rome a solid action game, albeit a bit repetitive.
The single player angle of Ryse come also with several collectables to be found scattered about the levels, which unlocks concept art and comics, and a multiplayer mode, which allows you to play what is basically a nerfed Marius against waves of enemies along with another player on few maps and some game modes (or even completely solo, should you prefer).
Even the multiplayer mode however doesn't offer any new gameplay novelty, aside from a set of new abilities a character can use during a match by choosing a certain god over another at the start and an equipment system, which is fueled by purchasing dedicated packs containing random items with the in-game currency by winning matches.
Ryse: Son of Rome is also a game that looks remarkably well and the various areas you get to visit (as well as the characters populating them) are indeed gorgeous and a solid point in favor of the game. But if that, along with a nice but pretty average gameplay, is enough to warrant a purchase is entirely up to you

If you were in elementary school during the 1980's, you might just be old enough to remember floppy disks, Apple DOS, and the frightening noises that those old disk drives used to make when reading. You may also remember the scores of educational video games designed to teach spelling, math, history, and/or hygene; most not particularly fun or memorable.
Influent is the bad♥♥♥♥♥nephew of the old educational games that used to put us to sleep in 4th grade. The gameplay is super-straightforward, click your way around a five room apartment and click on objects to hear the names pronounced in a different language than you are used to. After a while of doing this, you'll assemble a vocabulary list, and you can set yourself up to go back through the apartment and match the words with the objects.
Something important to understand going in; Influent is not actually a *language* tutor, tt's a vocabulary tutor. It does teach parts of speech, offer synonyms, pronounce words, and if the language in question has multiple alphabets, it can be toggled between them. You'll be able to associate the words with a picture, and since the apartment is pretty well organized (No spare set of sneakers in the fridge,) you'll be able to form easier or harder vocab lists by choosing from different kinds of items. (A very easy one might include only items in the bathroom, while a hard one will have you running all over the apartment.)
Influent won't actually teach sentence structure, detail word usage, or explain phrasing. As such, this is probably best used with a language that you speak a little of, but need to improve fluency with. (As opposed one you don't know anything about at all.)
It's sort of like video flash cards on horse steroids, and as far as that goes, it accomplishes it pretty damn well.

If you do buy this, make sure you understand what you're getting into before purchase. Even though it says 'Learn [Language]', it really means learn vocabulary. There is no context or detailled examples, conjugation, phrasing, or anything else you need to use the vocabulary you get. The adjectives and verbs are sometimes related to the object, but other times the relationship is just bad: computer is linked to intelligent and television is linked to stupid. If you change a noun to a synonym, the linked adjective/verb still use the old noun as the hint.
But what it does do is make learning vocabulary by repetition less tedious because of the 'game' presentation. There are some times when items are small and easy to misclick (like the pen and pencil) unless you spend time zooming in or stabilizing your mouse. The airplane reward is novel at first but it wore off quickly and I returned to human mode.
I'd recommend something like DuoLingo for a more comprehensive (and free) alternative, but even that isn't a replacement for real world learning or classes. However, one thing you get here that you can't get elsewhere is the ability to go into first person, stare into the mirror and gaze into your character's soulless, unblinking eyes.

But it's such a nice experience that it doesn't matter. The dialogue seems a bit trite to begin with (and to be fair, is a bit stilted at times, with the odd sentence that sounds like it's been badly translated) but you soon grow to like it, and the story can go in one of several directions based on your choices. There aren't that many backdrops or characters altogether, but the art and music are so wonderful that it's really a pleasure to play through.
Overall, I'd highly recommend this; it's just such a nice experience. Don't buy it, though, if you're expecting action, or puzzles, or a game - it isn't really any of those things. It's more like you're in the audience for a mysterious and beautiful piece of theatre that makes you feel like a little child listening to a storyteller.

In total, the game is pretty straight forward and good. The victory conditions and controls for game rules are unique and are, at least to me, the main draw for this game vs over 4X games. However, there is one area where the game feels like it falls flat: combat. Combat happens in a pseudo-simulataneous turn layout that, to me, feels exceptionally clunky and manual control is poorly implemented. A combat turn begins with you issuing general commands to individual units and once you hit go, the turn executes for all units on both sides of the conflict with faster units moving first. The problem with this setup is that if any other unit moves into the area you instructed a unit to move to, it disregards the order and re-assigns to whatever order the AI feels is the most important move. It would have been just as easy to begin a turn, rotating through the units in order of speed and issuing individual commands that execute and complete before moving onto the next unit in the turn. Instead, they threw this tried and true system to the wind to create this clunky, chaotic and often times infuriating system in which the actual player does interacts tactically with his units very little and the computer basically controls the entire flow of combat.
Overall I'd give the game a 7/10.

Endless Space was a great game, not ground-breaking but very well made, managing to bring some new ideas despite being a sort-of-a copy of previous 4x Space games. The races while all different from each other, had many similarities to other Space Fantasy races we had seen before.
When Endless Legend was announced; truth be told I only expected a simple background change to the Endless Space game we already had. Perhaps just moving from space to a single planet but keeping the core gameplay the same.
That is to some extent true; those familiar with Endless Space will find themselves at home here, city management, hero skills and army interface all remind us of Endless Space, the overall style of the UI is also very similar.
However what makes this game fascinating and special is the amount of detail in it and the amazing atmosphere. Every single race is unique, not only in gameplay but in background and story; even their interactions with the basic currency of the game. This small gameplay element "currency" changes the morals and customs of these peoples.
There are Empire-stories, world-stories, minor faction-stories and all of them are told through quests that remind us of RPG classics. For the single World of Auriga; the developers managed to put in more story than all the systems in Endless Space ever had.
Visuals are amazing, colourful but not cartoonish, absolutely cheerful and pleasing to look at, despite being a turn based game, I have never felt bored or disinterested, even during the periods of waiting for friends to complete their turns.
The final and dearest point has to be the music; I can safely say that this game has the best or at least one of the best soundtracks I have ever had the pleasure to listen to. I have played it more than a day now in total and every track still takes me on an emotional journey. The use of Guitar tones together with the Harp is especially noteworthy. The fact that the Devs provide it for free is also much appreciated, would be well worth a fee to download.
Despite the welcome popularity of 4x and strategy games causing a bit of a surplus of such games to pick from: I very much recommend this game to anyone that enjoys good strategy and story.

It's like Civ, but it's fantasy. You've probably worked that out by now.
There are a few really nice features that make it stand out more to me than Civ 5 did. First, the world is split into regions. Plonk a city down in a region and that region is yours, as are all the resources in that region (if you have the technology and buildings to harvest them). This means that you don't have to put down cities in awkward places just to secure your border, or nab a particularly important resource, which is a definite plus point. The combat is also vastly better than Civ, with a nice tactical map system when armies clash. Then there's the quest system, which nudges you towards exploration and towards playing according to your faction's theme. For example, the Wild Walkers get quests to build up cities, while the murderous Cultists get quests to raze cities and subdue minor factions. But it never feels intrusive, and the rewards are worthwhile. Overall the game has definitly got that Civ "one more turn" effect - I missed lunch today because I couldn't stop!
That said, there are a few things I'd criticise the it for. Firstly it does a terrible job of explaining itself, especially the victory conditions. My second play through I won a Supremecy victory, and I really have no idea what that even meant. I mean, sure I'd beaten the other factions into the ground, but the victory seemed to come out of nowhere. Secondly, the AI seem a bit passive - in my first play through I was hopelessly sandwiched between vastly more powerful factions who could have wiped me off the map very quickly, but all of them accepted peace treaties and alliances, and pretty soon I was running my own little UN; not a single war happened until one of the AI factions was close to an economic victory and I got everyone to declare war on them. That said, in my second play through, where I played aggressively, several factions were wiped out before I even met them, so perhaps the AI are more keen to go to war with each other than the player. Thirdly, the AI difficulty seems badly tuned. My first play through was on normal difficulty and the AI racked up well over 10x my score, and I was nowhere near any victory conditions by the end (when an AI won). So I dropped it down a level to easy, where the AI bumbles around hopelessly and is pretty much a punching bag in war. The difference between the two difficulties is pretty radical to say the least.
As an aside, be prepared to do a lot of fiddling around to get it to run on Windows 10. I had to set it to run in Windows 7 compatibility mode with admin permissions and no Steam overlay before it would even get past the first loading screen.
Overall I'd recommend it to any fans of Civ, even people who, like myself, found the last Civ game disappointing.

The basics are the same: there is a map (actually, many maps in this case) with multiple lanes connecting two bases to each other, and from your base automatic minions march forward to the other base, trying to destroy it. There are towers on each lane, defending the bases, and you choose a champion to play with to assist your miniature army and in the end, destroy the enemy base. Characters are unique and fun to play, and there are a lot interesting mechanisms thanks to the 2D platformer enviroment. The learning curve is very user friendly, nothing like LoL or DotA2 where you need to spend countless hours, days, weeks, even months to learn and experience all the matchups, get used to the itemization system and everything. You still level up, you still buy "items" (it's merged with skill leveling at level ups), but it takes 5-10 minutes, a half hour top to get used to the system and the characters, and it's not getting boring at all later on. A must have for everyone who likes the genre but can't / don't want to afford the time it takes to really get into it. It's on sale for ridicolously low price pretty often on various sites, so keep your eyes open!

A wonderfully inventive game, Evoland features a mixture of game play between the Legend of Zelda series and the Final Fantasy series. You start out with only black and white, 2 dimensional game play. You unlock colors, graphics, 3 dimensional gameplay, sound and sound quality, gameplay features and basically everything to do with a game by finding the different and many chest found throughout the game.
It also features (true to the Final Fantasy spirit), a mini card game within the game. You can find or buy cards to play it. A fun plot (once you unlock the storyline as you do everything else including basic movement), it keeps you entertained for hours. You also unlock the ability of save points found scattered throughout the land, health (which when in Zelda mode shows as hearts in the upper right hand side of the screen). When in Final Fantasy open world exploration mode with radom encounters, battles play out as made famous by the Final Fantasy series up to Final Fantasy IX.
More unlocks and fun than you can imagine, the gameplay is highly addictive and keeps you smiling. Dungeons also unfold where you must move blocks onto pressure pads to open gates or put you in trap rooms where you must defeat all the monsters within to escape, and mazes unfold as well. I could not for the price range recommend many games as highly as this one for absolutely any gamers collection. On a scale of 1 to 10, 1 being horrible and 10 being the most awesome game of all time, this one would rank as a solid 9. Well worth the investment.

Fist of Awesome exceeded my expectations.
I was expecting it to be completely terrible, but it's actually not...No wait...ehhh yeah it's still pretty bad.
This game is extremely repetitive and slow. Part of what keeps a beatemup fresh is the diversity of the enemies and levels. While the locales change and the bears get different clothes, they never graduate out of the same tired move-sets and patterns. Let's use Streets of Rage 2 as an example. There could be jet-pack bears, bears with electric whips, ninja-bears, robot-bears, and so on. All of these enemies would require a different approach. Also the enemy life-bars get far too long. It's not like there is any real strategy. Punch the bear three times, kick them in the nuts, punch them three times, repeat until they die. It's sometimes necessary to move around, use back-attacks, and keep the bears "herded" for easy disposal. At least the developer got this aspect right.
I'm not sure if it's an issue with the art-design or what, but beating enemies up, just isn't satisfying. It seems to me that there's not enough oomph. Wait. What the heck is "oomph"? When you're playing Final Fight 1 and Haggar picks up a thug and pile-drives him into the ground, there's this deep bass that is oomph as heck. When a fist the size of a basketball connects with an enemy's face, there has to be a high level of oomph-ness. Fist of Awesome feels like everyone is just play-fighting. Almost all of the sound-effects sound like they were made by some guy with a microphone. It's a cute idea, but it doesn't really work. The massive life-bars also represent a lack of oomph because you have to punch everyone 50 times. Something as simple as some different animations, better throws, or even a decent jump-kick would have done wonders.
Still, Fist of Awesome isn't completely terrible. The music is great, the arena is interesting (you have to use specific moves or you'll run out of time), and the mechanics are functional. I've played a number of horrendous beatemups on Steam, so I'm thrilled when even the most basic aspects of the game actually work.
Not nearly thrilled enough to recommend this game though. There are literally hundreds of better options if you're looking for a beatemup.

Gameplay 9/10:

The only problem here is the zombie mode's the normal pvp zombies is fun but when playing as a zombie you can look like a disabled carrot while moving as you take damage.
Graphics 6/10:
The graphics are crap but still good for a nice nostalgia trip, they used the default cs 1.6 map textures, but I cannot pinpoint the gun models, some are new (mp5) and some are 1.6 and CZ (Awp)
Content 10/10:
When you buy a game you expect a ton of content, many games don't give that but CSN:Z gives that for free. Tons of weapons/features/items and more, nuff said.
Customization 9.5/10:
Nobody buys a CS game for the purpose of customization only, but CSN:Z is a game you would expect to give customization and it does.
Settings 6.5/10:
Not high amounts of options but enough needed for a game like this.
Nostalgia 10/10:
Included in CSN:Z is CS 1.6 for free
Verdict 8.2/10:
Great job Nexon you made a f2p fps that is not p2w, you made a zombie game relatively original and a zombie game that  has the ability to do something that is not zombies and CS 1.6 for free.

The game is a direct fresh continuation from the previous lego batman games with returning characters liek superman, joker, lex luthor and a lot more. Plus the whole justice league. Now this game feature the new 52 style reboot version of the characters so most of the costumes are comic accurate. Now they did return one fan favorite thing from lego marvel superheroes. Its the big figures. Now bane can turn into the full sized bane we always wanted him to be. Also solomon grundy and killer croc finally look size appropriate. All controls are exactly the same and they finally added xbox controller support but its a bit hard to configure at first because you dont know what action is which until you test it. If you have a ps3 controller like me, it will also work but your program needs to configure it to have programs to recognize it as an xbox controller layout. So using DS3 tool is very helpful. Story wise its spit into 3 large acts. The first one is slowly assembling the justice league while trying to stop groups of bad guys. The lex and joker team up returns as lex tries to hack into the watchtower to become president by trying to use its lazer to threaten earth to vote for him. You with your team has to stop him with their other bad guys. Its fun and levels arent too puzzling. The second act is teaming up with lex and jokers team to stop brainiac from shrinking earth to the size of a basketball. This act is a bit slow and kinda drags on. Just as they mention a major battle or when you think its the final fight after a decent amount of build up, the game just throws in filler missions that just make it feel like a bit of a chore and you feel like rushing the levels at this point. Once you finally beat braniac in the longest mission ever (too long), you actually dont finish the game. This is where act 3 comes up. You need to now collect all 6 major lantern corps lantern crystals. This is where they sorta introduce their selling point of the game. You have to travel to each planet that is home to the lantern and fight through a level to reach the final boss fight which some were boring but some were fun. Then you have to go back to earth to resize earth from being half shrunken by brainiac already, but by resizing earth, you resized the trap you used to hold brainiac for 6 WHOLE MISSIONS. HOW DOESNT HE ESCAPE! But anyways he escapes and you go the supermans fortress of solitude to combine the crystals to resize earth more. Now brainiac comes and mind controls superman and makes him a giant and you have to stop him. Simple fun fight and bam the story ends. So the story is entertaining enought to want to see what happens in the end. Now there are 150 characters not including dlc ones and i feel like its a bit of a let down after lego marvel had 140 characters not including dlc and all they did was add 10 more. I felt like they could have done more especially since a lot were the same from lego batman 2. Unlocking most of the characters required you to find the character tokens either by doing these new things called quests where you talk to people around the hubs (free roam areas) and finding stuff for them. Or you can try to solve puzzles to collect them. Travelling back to the 6 planets are sorta fun when you first get there but after a bit the music and collectability makes it hard to get all the unlockables there expecially if you want a gold brick by following green loontern (the duck from looney toons) to give you a whole 360 tour of the planet. Some characters have some interesting characteristics like for example with shazam. When you choose him, he is actually billy batson and you area actually a minifig kid running around with no powers. Then by pressing the y button, triangle key, or whatever its on the keyboard, he yells SHAZAM! and a lightning bolt hits him and hes shazam. That cool. They do something with superman also where you can transform into clark kent by pressing the same button and he flies out of the screen and returns as clark in his reporter outfit all scrawny. Its cool because he can use heatvision and when you do he pulls down his glasses and uses it. Nice attention to detail there. The he can transform back by pressing the button and a telephone booth appears and he rips his suit open a little like he does as he suits up and jumps in the booth and out comes superman! Red brick are still here so you can still get your cheats on which is fun. I havent unlocked all of them but i feel they will be the same as preivious games. Graphics are upscale a bit more with beter textures, realistic glossy lego figures, better lighting effects with sligh light shafts which are very appreciated. So in the end i would rate this game a 7-8 out of 10 because of  its replayability value and if youre a fan of the franchise, it does it honor. Plus you are rewarded with a huge fan service nostalgia level that recreates the batman 1966 tv show senarios with the adam west batman and voiced by him. They even add those comic sounds like BANG, FWOOSH, FTWANg, and more with the text popping up everytime you hit something. So its a recommended game id say. btw conan o brien can be a pest and you will se if you get it.

As I write this review the Arrow DLC still has yet to drop so I'm basing this on having 100% this game with the current three dlcs out with the season pass.  First and foremost let me say how much I hated the storyline in this game.  For me it was the  worst of all the lego games I've played (the other Batmans, Harry Potter, Marvel, Indiana Jones, Pirates of the Caribbean, Lego Movie).  I will admit my biggest problem is that I'm not a big DC person.  I only like a few characters and Batman is one of them so when I buy a game called Lego Batman I expect the storyline to be promeniently about Batman.  This wasn't that.  This was Lego Green Lantern or Lego DC Universe but it wasn't Lego Batman.  I realize that they probably called it that to make more money but it really irks me.  Don't get me wrong I still had fun with the game, as I do with all the lego games.  I was just really looking forward to a batman centric story.  That being said I did not run into as many glitches as others have complained about.  I also played this game with the XBOX wired controller for Windows and never had a single problem with the controls as some other people have said.  The controller worked fine for me and I played all nearly 70 hours with it.
These are the glitches that I did run into however:
-The bat computer doesn't work in the bat cave to allow you to see levels and replay them even though Conan says it does.
-When you run over a heart after taking out an enemy it doesn't always add a heart to your meter if you are low.  This is a problem I also noticed in Lego Marvel but not as prevalent as here.
-When I was free playing the level Lantern Menance the game crashed on me three times.  There wasn't a checkpoint before each crash so I lost everything each time.  I had to save and exit a few times as well as start at a different point in the level then go back before I could get everything.  The game never crashed before or after this.  Only when I free played this level.
-Some of the Quests glitched in various ways.
-The rest were standard Lego glitches that are pretty much in every game.
Ok so I guess this is where I'll go through my pros and cons:
Pros:
-All the suits in this game can be accessed by holding down the Y button if you're using a controller, once you find the corresponding token.  Makes things a lot easier when you need different suits, also if you place the character by where they need to do the suit change sometimes you can just hit the B button and it will automatically change to the suit you need.  I liked this a lot better than the previous games.
-The Bonus Batman '66 level and the DLC levels which I enjoyed more than the game itself.  There's a lot of fun stuff there. Totally can't wait for the Arrow, Bizarro and Suicide Squad DLCs.
-Geoff Johns, Jim Lee, Kevin Smith, Adam West and the Green Loontern are playable characters which is just awesome.
-That they shut up Conan O'Brien in the last update so he only speaks if you walk up to him and hit the B button.  He's incessent talking was annoying before but you may want to talk to him the first time through just to get the lay of the land.
-managed to finish the entire game in two weeks and sixty-seven hours which isn't bad for a lego game.
-Voice acting was fun and good as it usually is since they started letting the characters speak.
-There are a plenty of characters in this game so have ample combinations for free play, quests and races
-There are many places to visit with quests and races including the bat cave (which has a room modeled after the batman tv show), the hall of justice, the watchtower, the seven lantern planets and a moon base
-Each free play level is broken up into different sections so you don't necessarily have to start from the beginning
-You can find unlocked red bricks in both the bat cave and the watchtower by going to the trophy room.  Much of what's in the watchtower is also in the bat cave so you can decide where you want to go.
Cons:
-This game has the fewest checkpoints I've ever seen for a lego game. This became a problem when I went on to free play as I mentioned above
-Couldn't access any free play levels or characters that were unlocked until after you got so far into the story.  Once you were done with the story you could access unlocked vehicles in Oa, unlocked characters by holding down the Y button or visiting one of the Lantern planets and free play levels from the control room in the watchtower.  It could sometimes be annoying to go from one to the other just to unlock something, especially since the bat computer didn't work.
-The map wasn't as good as Lego Marvel and when you got past a certain level in story mode you kept going back to the control room and had to find your next level on it.  I really didn't like that, it was a bit obnoxious.
-there are no extra hearts or invincible red bricks in this game, which could have been useful, but there's a ghost stud collector... except there is almost no ghost studs in this game.  Pretty stupid.
-VR Missions- I really hated these.  Almost threw my controller at my monitor a few times.  Need to do them to get some characters, vehicles and gold bricks though as well as complete a few missions. Was glad when they were done.
Overall I like the game and do recommend it though I wish there was more batman but I believe the dlcs in this game surpass anything they've done in the others and I can't wait to play them all.  Below are some tips and suggestions if you are not the kinda person who likes that stuff stop reading here.
Tips and suggestions:
-I found the red bricks for the gold brick detector, quest detector & adam west in peril detector were very useful on the hub planets
-If you are like me and like to get all the achievements then to get some of them do the following things: visit all the hub planets on a single gaming session; Jump on something 50 times in a row; the one with Krypto in the Man of Steel level you have to change both characters to Krypto; When you are in the control room there is a room to the right which you will need to go in for two of the achievements.
-Wait until you're done with story mode to do free play, it's just easier
-I found doing quests and stuff area by area worked best.
-On your way to Oa for the first time inspect the moon instead of going through the grate. There's an achievement with cows that isn't too hard to find.
-When in Oa I used the cars for the land races (Flash's Car worked best for me) but I used flying characters for all the air races because the planes flew like junk.  You just got to find the right one to use (Zatanna, Red Torando were among the ones that worked best for me) and may also have to boost the character in flight when the gates are farther apart.
-Zatanna is good character to use on things because she can fly, blow up gold objects and go through grates.  Cyborg is also cool cause once you have the space suit when you double jump with him (no matter what suit he's currently wearing) he'll switch to the space suit and fly.
Well if you've read all this you must have had a lot of time on your hands lol.  Thanks for reading and good luck!

As the first of Moacube's visual novels,
is a roaring success both for its genre and as an example of literary deconstruction. I've been meaning to play this game for years, and now I did, I cannot stop myself from taking new playthroughs to unlock all ending variants, to see what else this game may have in store for me. This unconventional interpretation of the classical folktale
breaks all stereotypes and social generalizations, presenting an in-depth analysis of all its characters and probable intervening dynamics. Kudos to the developer upfront!
At this point, everyone with a semi-European cultural understanding is familiar with the story of Cinderella. Poor, golden hearted young woman who is treated like a slave in her own home by her ambitious stepmother and evil stepsisters. All her kindness only meets with mistreatment until a fairy godmother appears to bless her with a magical dress, a pumpkin carriage and glass slippers to attend the ball of the Prince. There, she is to steal Prince's heart with a glance and become the queen of the kingdom after a short pursuit involving those glass slippers. There, happily ever after, right? Nope, not so much. The original story was a brutal one compared to the Disney-fied version anyhow, and with
now, we are in for a more realistic version of the old fairytale.
Here, our protagonist' conditions are more or less the same with the original story. Her father has passed away, and now she is living with her stepmother and two stepsisters, whom treat her little better than a servant. She wishes to change her life, take the control of her future and decide the outcome of her own story though, rather than waiting for magic to happen! Sure, waiting for magic to happen is still our option, but just one of our options nonetheless. We are to live through a week of Cinders to witness the events just before the guard captain of his majesty knocks on our door. What happened to present such a necessity? Now, that is gonna be our choice. We will create a Cinders of our own. We'll make various choices, pick how to act towards whom and what to pursue in the way we chose. Eventually, we will meet one of the various endings appropriate for our personality.
In this glamorous visual novel, every single choice sincerely matters. Our actions determine our romance option - yup, we don't have to go happily ever after with the prince - , our character and eventually our own ending. Every single character involving - whether their role in the original story were small or grand - are reimagined into actual people, with their own personalities, background and aspirations. Did you ever think why the stepmother treated Cinderella the way she did? Just because she was evil? Or did you ever take a second glance at the captain of the guards? Why the fairy actually aided our girl the way she did? Because that's what fairies are supposed to do? Definitely not! Here, you are presented with a decent analysis of the story, stripped away from its embellishment and take a realistic approach to the situation, wrapped in genuine medieval context. The result is an incredible story with layers of characterization and perfect narrative with philosophical value.
The display is topnotch. All the artwork - both characters and the environment are fitting for a fairytale alright. Yet, this is not the strongest suit of the display. All character CG are presented in a way to maintain noteworthy body language and facial mimics, fortifying the narrative furthermore. Add a breathtaking soundtrack with various instrumental pieces of folk and epic music, and voila: here is a display environment you wouldn't grow tired of playing over and over again.
Now, I've already noted that endings are various. There are mainly 4 endings: one fairytale, one lady of the house, one “whatever, I'm out of this place" and one "not so happy". All these endings carry their own varieties within themselves however. According to the romance you pursue, the way you treated people and the amount of information you managed to gather by the end, you'll get a different variety of these endings. Every one of them can be tracked and re-read in the menu too.
At the end,
is one of the most imaginative, deep and successfully displayed visual novels that I've ever played. Even if you are not a fan of the genre, you may enjoy this one thanks to its narrative quality, depth and even sense of humor! At this point, I'll be looking forward for any VN that Moacube would throw my way. Enjoy!

Do you want to pay money for a game with an underlying narrative about how abusers are kinda right and abuse victims should feel bad for taking appropriate action?  No amount of witty dialogue could cover up the inherently bad-- and at times disturbing-- game writing.
The game promised to add character depth to a familiar story, and it did-- to a point.  The stepsisters have a dynamic consistent with being raised by a manipulative, abusive mother who plays them against each other.  Lady Carmosa, the stepmother, is emotionally abusive in a realistic way.  Like many abusive people, she makes sure to micromanage the people that she's abusing, put them down, and try tell them constantly that they need her to treat them this way because of how pitiful/stupid/etc. they are.  Cinders mentions in the dialogue that she believes that Lady Carmosa is capable of killing, and it's implied in Carmosa's dailogue that she may have killed her second husband, so she represents a physical danger as well.
There's a point in the dialogue where Cinders is speaking to someone who knew her late mother.  It has already been established that her stepmother is abusive.  Cinders explains that she believes that she-- not her stepmother-- is the legal inheritor of the family estates.  I chose the option for wanting to get an attorney to get my house back.  Mom's friend promptly gave me a guilt trip about the "consequences" of such a harsh act when my stepmother was just keeping the family fortune together.  You know, the family fortune that wasn't even legally hers that she's only using to benefit herself.  Given the more realistic take on abuse dynamics that the writers had so far, I figured that this was intentional.  Abuse victims often hear similar things from third parties about why their husband/parent/etc. isn't such a bad person and they should be grateful.  I waited for the protagonist to have an opportunity to confront this clearly inappropriate behaviour.
Nope.  Wasn't happening.
Every time the option for getting an attorney to get my (expletive) house back came up, I clicked it.  Every time, I got an NPC guilt trip and dialogue to make sure that I knew that-- although there are officially no wrong choices in this game-- I had made a wrong choice.  Bad, BAD player wanting people to get stolen property back from their abuser through appropriate legal channels.  How could I!  No matter how many times you choose that option, you will not have the opportunity to seek legal assistance to get the family house which you believe you're the legal inheritor of back.  There's also this little bit of talking to herself that Cinders has about how she's materially better off than most of the women in town so maybe she should be grateful for the life that her stepmother has given her.  You know, because if an abusive person takes our stuff we should be grateful to the abuser for what they've deigned to give us.
I played through the game just to be sure that there wasn't, you know, some upcoming branch in which the game would deal with the mess it made.  Nope.  It's sure as hell not getting a second play through.

An enjoyable take on the Cinderella tale, with sufficient twists and tweaks to continue making everything interesting.
The plots' decent enough, the characters are relateable, and the artwork is simply gorgeous. All in all, quite enjoyable.

As established in earlier reviews, the world is beautiful; an appropriate art style and score. I appreciated that it focuses on the consequences of your character's developing personality, which you decide through dialogue and action choices, instead of focusing narrowly on the expected romantic relationship with "Cinderella's" prince.
Some previous reviews criticized how the game punishes you monotonously for choosing "the wrong" character development choices. However, with that in mind, I noticed that the very 1st scene of the game, which foreshadows later events, hints at your win objective: your characters wonders if having a better relationship with the others in her life and making more empathetic yet pragmatic choices would have been better for her in the long-run. So, it's insinuated that the game will reward you for exploring her curiosity; punishing you when you're too romantic or too prejudiced.
But, there are issues with the game. It's fair for some to be disappointed that the game doesn't have good and bad ending for all the possible character arcs--romantic, headstrong, or pragmatic--when it invests so much in immersing you in the world and having you feel like you are the protagonist. It feels like the game is attacking you; not just the character you created. Also, if you have little tolerance for it, the overt callbacks to the original fairy tale by the protagonist and morality play can feel like it's hitting you over the head mercilessly. But, if you come in wanting what the adventure offers, it's good at what it intended to do.

A few things to expect if you buy Awesomenauts:
The matchmaking issues have never been fixed.  There is no unranked play.  You frequently get matched in to ongoing games.  When the community is at its usual height (meaning not during a sale) you will very frequently get dropped in to matches that are well beyond lost.  Quitting out and re-queuing will often get you dropped right back in to the same FUBAR match.  You'll find yourself playing with bots against a premade team more often than 'naut.
When there is not a sale, a majority of the active players are very experienced.  They will let you know that power creep has made many of the base characters pretty useless.  Without Starstorm, you'll find yourself on the receiving end of a lot of beatings.  There are a couple of base characters that see a good amount of high-end play, but ask yourself if you really plan to commit that much time to this game.  The pool of honestly useful characters is pretty limited.
There are no dedicated servers. There are no region settings.   This results in a lot of games where ping will be 200 or greater.  You'll be stuttering around slowly while the other team ruins your day.  And it will happen a lot.
I've not played with the Overdrive expansion, but I don't see any of its characters topping any leaderboards.
I've seen plenty of rumblings that the new XP system causes some real matchmaking inequality.  Remember, there is no unranked play.  The learning curve of any MOBA is pretty steep, and it gets much worse when you're stuck in a constant stream of losing matches with only bots on your team to teach you.
If you can overlook these faults, the game is mechanically sound and visually appealing.  The original music is mostly pretty great.

This game is basically a forum troll in game form: something terrible and without merit that is trying to get attention it doesn't deserve.
The game: The controls are terrible and later in the game they introduce platforming that you have to get through to proceed, using those same atrocious controls. Imagine precision jumping on tiny platforms, in floaty 3D environments, with sloppy tank controls. Also you can't see your feet, or your shadow. Every landing is a guess, and sometimes platforms just drop you anyway if you're too close to the edge.
The narrator: The on again/off again narrator is verbally abusive throughout, offers no insight, and is just annoying every time he chimes in. He's basically just there to threaten to kill you if you don't play along. That's it. No wit, no humor, no insight, no point.
Level design: The levels don't take the game's own setting into account and the level design just devolves and gets lazier the further you go, and the "twist" at the end reveals that you never left reality, so those "lazy dream world" levels make no sense.
The plot: The entire story, if one can call it that, is just an immature and juvenile mess. It is revealed in its entirety at the end of the game, in the visually deprived ending sequence. By this I don't mean you are lead down a trail of hints to piece everything together at the end. No, you are just lead through levels at literal gun point and told the story ONLY when you reach the end of the game. And it's not worth the effort. It's sloppy writing the likes of a 15 year old trying to be edgy would write. You're just some dude and your girlfriend's step father kidnaps you, puts you through hell(somehow), all because apparently, you and your girlfriend are blood relatives... He kidnapped someone, held them captive against their will, threatened their lives (and murder them if you take into account the fact he kills you if you fail any of the badly laid out task he throws at you, some of which are entirely based on GUESSING.) and his reason is "I didn't want you to have sex with your sister"... then how about just telling him they are related? In fact, she girl chimes in and says she just found out and was going to tell you, but her step dad kidnapped you first.
What was even the point.

This new LEGO game does it's best to look spectacular at it's highest, whilst staying optimised for older compters, I never not liked the graphics of LEGO games, and much like most of their playsets, they are more innovative with each generation. Having played Cinders for more than 40 hours (guess I was really that into the game lol), I had the chance to unlock all the trophies and possible variants. I wanted to do so before posting my review of Cinders, as I usually like to complete a game as much as I can before I write a review. XD
Anyway, as a fan of visual novel games, I'll be writing this review from that perspective. Without a doubt, Cinders is one of the best VNs I've had a chance of playing and this isn't an exaggeration. Upon starting a game, the first thing that one would notice right away is the art. It's absolutely beautiful, as though it came straight out of classic paintings. The art is different from those in other VNs in that it doesn't adopt the anime-style but because of the nature of the story, I believe it was a wise decision to steer away from the norm. The music as well was quite beautiful and I felt that it did fit for most of the characters. I only wish there had been a jukebox feature in the menu so players could have a chance to listen to various music pieces away from playing the game itself.
What ends up sealing the deal for me, though, is the story. A VN must have an engaging story that I feel as though I can immerse myself in. It takes the classic story of Cinderella but adds a new twist to it. The protagonist, Cinders, doesn't have to be the helpless girl abused by her stepmother and stepsisters. The player can make decisions which shape Cinders' personality so she can range anywhere from being naive to cunning to rebellious. I loved the various branches that the games takes the player through so there are so many possible paths that one can take.
If there are any negatives, though, I'd say that there were a few typos here and there. I noticed a few grammar errors as well as some inconsistencies between using the American and British version of English words but honestly, these negatives are so minor. Although it certainly couldn't hurt to have the mistakes polished a bit, Cinders is such a beautiful, wonderful game itself that I can overlook them.
I'm happy to see that Steam has made such a wonderful VN available to its community and I hope to see many more games from MoaCube in the future. ^^

Overall, Cinders was a joy to play. Some loveable characters, incredible art, charming music, and a fun retelling of Cinderella.
Game Elements: First and foremost, Cinders is a game. It offers many choices to influence the outcome of the game, and the outcomes themselves are varied enough to offer plenty incentive for multiple playthroughs. The skip mode is nicely implemented, as it stops automatically on text you haven't seen before. However, it doesn't really do anything unique for its genre.
Story and characters: It's good, but not great. Some fantastic character development with the sisters, but the love interests and the stepmother could use work.
---------------Spoilers Ahead!
Carmosa, the stepmother, as you could imagine, treats Cinders deplorably, but we aren't provided with much of a motive as to why she acts this way. Yes, Cinders is not a biological daughter, but that does not preclude Carmosa from treating Cinders with respect. What's more obnoxious about this is that the game writing hints to the player that we should understand Carmosa's actions and respect her for it! It's little things, however, that make this a contradictory stance for the game: Carmosa could have fed her daughters smaller portions of dinner rather than feeding Cinders cold scraps; Carmosa's daughters could wear cheaper dresses so Cinders could wear something other than rags. It does not make sense for Cinders to respect Carmosa in this game unless she forgets the way Carmosa has treated her, and so the Carmosa as advisor ending makes no sense.
Gloria and Sophie, however, are excellent characters with natural growth through the course of the game. Gloria is seemingly cruel but just trying to live up to her mother by copying her, and in the way loses herself; Sophie is bitter and cynical because Gloria and her mother constantly criticize her and so her self esteem is ruined. Cinders has the option to help both of them grow in the game by encouraging Gloria to explore her interests and encouraging Sophie to be proud of her intelligence and intellectualism. I was also impressed by their complex relationship with Carmosa, since they loved her for what she's done for them (climbing the social ladder so they could have a better life), but they also resent her for not letting them to be free to do as they wish. It culminates in the Grand Ball, where Sophie ultimately decides she doesn't want what her mother wants for her, and Gloria doesn't know if she wants it, either.
Now the love interests. Let's start with Tobias, the childhood friend. He's got plenty of enjoyable one-liners and pleasant dialogue, should you interact with him. However, I never learn to trust him quite as much as Cinders does in his romance route. He puts his business ethics before Cinders's trust, worrying that she might ruin his reputation as a merchant. This is not a good start to a loving, trusting relationship. He wants to run away with Cinders in order to help her out in the traveler arc, but it would have been nice for his character development if we knew of some reason that he would want to run away from it all, much as Cinders wanted to run away in the Perrault traveler route. Maybe Tobias couldn't stand living in his hometown anymore; maybe he's actually not as honest as he appears, and he has some shady business he's running away from. I think my favorite route for him is Cinders as a noblewoman that marries her, as it seems totally believable that he would lend her a lot of money for social events and later marry her since they're in the same town. I do not like him as a lover to Queen Cinders, but that's because I'm trying to piece how they would stay in contact at court before he becomes a count.
Oh, Perrault. So many conflicting feelings. My absolute favorite ending is Perrault as the lover to the Machiavellian Queen Cinders, as it is incredibly believable that she would continue to see him after she becomes queen. He's an interesting character, indecisive on whether he likes killing and duty, but he would be improved by being more human and less tropey. I believe the true happy ending is Cinders adventuring with Perrault, btw ;)
And the Prince. So much could have happened! He was a good character with lots of potential! But then he focused on Cinders's looks at the ball... I would've liked to see him spy on her after the ball to determine if she was truly smart, if he was so committed to personality. He just needed more. And he doesn't deserve any ending where he isn't happy. He has to have at least a few flaws!
I think the rest of the cast is sufficiently likeable, with the exception of Shady Character. He baffles me. Where'd he come from?
And finally, we have.... Cinders!! I love that she's so moldable depending on the player's actions. She can be aggressive and a trail-blazer, or she can be docile and simple. And the text is sufficiently clear that I know the outcome of my actions on Cinders's personality before they're revealed to me. A+.
-----End Spoilers----
Overall, Story is 7/10, and Characters are 6/10. There's a bit too much going on in plot and not enough going on in character reasoning/development for why they act the way they act.
Visuals and Sound
This is where the game shines. The art style is stunning! The characters are all beautiful, and the landscapes are all engrossing. For the average person, there's not much more to ask for. Now, from the perspective of an artist, there is more that could go into the art design. The characters suffer from what I like to call "Same Face Syndrome": they all have the same face and differ in how they dress. What if Perrault had a hooked nose? Or Sophie's lips were super thin and had no cupid's bow? This isn't a huge deal, but it is something that I would like to see addressed in future releases. And for a bonus: Tobias's left hand looks super weird.
The soundtrack is really fun and fitting, but there could be more sound effects to provide immersion.
Overall, Visuals are 8.5/10 and Sound is 7/10.
Enjoyment
Despite its flaws, it's still a very enjoyable game and a gem in the visual novel genre. I went and replayed it for all the different endings! I'd give it a total 7/10.

Sonic And Sega All-Stars Racing is a racing game that features some of the characters from Sega games. It was developed by Sumo Digital, who also made Outrun 2, and released in 2010. You can also call it kart racing, since it has all those weapons and powerups, but eh. You can. One things for sure: it's drift and boost based. It was also released on other consoles and iOS.
As usual, game supports either keyboard or XBox360 controller. It will still show keboard layout no matter what. Also, Steam/PC version is pretty barebones. For some reason, Sega decided that it shouldn't support any online feature. No Steam achievement. There is no Internet multiplayer, only local one. So most of you will be racing only against AI. There are no exclusive characters, like X360 version had Banjo-Kazookie. And there are no DLC, meaning that there is no Metal Sonic or Shenmue hero in forklift.
So, what you will get is racing game. Imagine colorful characters of Sonic and heroes of games like Billy Hatcher, AiAi or the ever grinning B. D. Joe. There are around twenty of them, with eight unlocked by default. And then you got the awesome varied tracks, which may have drifty like Casino Park from Sonic, have 90-degree turns and be riddled with obstacles like Monkey Ball tracks, or just be spooky Curien Mansion. Which is censored or alternative name for House of The Dead. Now, pour in weapons and add in drifting mechanic. And then add modes like Grand Prix, Missions, Time Attack. And add in Shopping where you can unlock characters, stages and music tracks for Sega Miles that you get for successfully completing races.
Characters vary in venichles that they drive. Outside of the usual stats differences, their vehicles can be sorted into few categories. First, there are usual cars, that can be divided into light and heavy ones. Then you got flying vehicles, like Tails Tornado, that aren't affected by terrain, like snow. And then you will get bikes, which are fast and you can get boost easily by performing ground trick, of pressing up and then down. Seriously, bikes are probably the best, not even sure if it's so balanced. And yes, once again, stats change, vehicles have different acceleration and handling, and, for example, some may stay in air after jump long enough to perform multiple tricks while other are too heavy to stay in air for long.
At least, thankfully, all the various tracks will catter to different vehicle types. Some are more straight, some will reward handling.
To little geniuses who wonder why Sonic has car: game itself has info in Sonic's profile that he drives a car to give other a sporting chance. The end.
And yes, tricks. This game heavily uses drifting mechanics and rewards you for drifting with boost. Drifting is very controllable there, you can take any turns with it or can even try to drift on straight road with some success. Though, you may want to release gas button for sharp turns. You can build up to three level of boost, that will activate after you release the drift button. I recommend you to release it as soon as you see three levels of boost and then drift again immeditly, there are some turns where you can do it twice!
You also will be rewarded with boost for doing tricks. First, at the start of race, during countdown, you have to start the gas somewhere between "3" and "2". Depends on each character. There are air tricks that anybody can do, you just have to press drift button while in air. But make sure to finish air trick before landing, otherwise you will lose all boost that was built up. Bikes, as said, also got ground trick where you just press up and down around.
Boosting will also knock obstacles down, like balls, giant casino chips and zzzzzzoooooombies.
The game also got power-ups that are randomly chosen when you pick it up. It got a fairly standard package of them. Speeding up, bombs, rockets, rainbow that only colors screen for real players, but hits AI characters. You can also shoot boxing gloves and rockets back. Actually, you can knock off the incoming rockets by using weapon of your own, usually by shooting it back. What kind of powerps you get also depends on what place you are in. As for stopping players that managed to get really far in the first place, it got usual "screw you" shooting star. The futher you are in the back, the more likely you will get good ones, getting triple rockets, or nuke rocket that you can detonate any time after launch.
Oh, and they got all-star moves. If you are really lacking behind you may get All-Star weapon. Announcer will not be afraid to tell it to everybody either. It's really a jolly power-up, as it will not only boost you to allow you to possibly get into the top, but it gives a character-specific spin. Akira from Virtua Fighter will hit his Outrun-like car with dashing elbow. Alex Kidd will ride on his helicopter, being able to shoot little shiny missiles. And Opa-Opa from Fantasy Zone will even lets you choose one of the three power-ups to use in this case. It shows off a great characters, variety and each one will play a short theme song.
You also got around 64 challenges to beat. What should I say, they are varied, changing between more standard ones and more of wacky. In one challenge you have to beat all Jet Set Radio Future tracks. In another you will beat up a huge zombie boss. Jolly.
And yes, you can also unlock music tracks. You can then choose to play any one of them in tracks, making it more varied than having same song in all Billy Hatcher tracks. Pretty much all of music is taken from previous games. The only unique ones in the game are main theme "So much more" and some other tracks used for menues, that sounds quite what you expect to hear from 90s racing games.
And since AI is the only opponent you will most likely get, he should be mentioned. You can disable "catch-up" in options, but I would not recommend you to do this. AI just isn't strong enough to figure out how to stop you if you will be far in the lead. It actually manages to drag itself down, as the last players will keep doing All Star move that will hit main pack but will usually fail to reach the top. So, really, let this option be, it doesn't rubberband strong enough to screw you up without reason. you can still stay in the lead, it's just that single mistake will get you back into main pack of racers.
Ai isn't that hard either. I was actually surprised that I managed to beat all the Advanced Grand Prix. And I was expecting it to be brutal at it's best. But I guess they tried to kept it fair.
AI also playes pretty well, althrough there are some constant thing about it. Some characters are better than others. Some drag behind.
For sure, most of the time you will be seeing Shadow The Hedgehog on his bike on top. And you will learn to hate him, as he keeps popping up on top and getting on second place in Grand Prix, where you will even want to pay extra attention to drag him down too, so you will have more breathing air in total scoring. Bonanza Bros also somehow manage to stay on top.
And then you got characters like Big and Eggman who keep staying in the last places and spam their All-Stars move. ARK: Survival of The Fittest suffers from a plethora of issues that need to be adressed before it can finally reach the potential it has.

For every good mechanic in ARK, there's a bad mechanic to off-set it. For instance, the game gives players a wide variety of strategies to utilize, from crafting high-end weapons to taming dinosaurs. Unfortunately, with the immense size of the arena, encountering players before the final 5-10 minutes is unlikely, unless you know the popular spots on the map. Taming dinos seems to be the best strategy right now, since teching leaves a lot to be desired in terms of equipment. At best, unless a Fabricator is made, you can have a basic shotgun, a basic pistol, and a basic rifle. The equipment degradation on these weapons is perhaps a bit too fast, as it almost forces techers to construct back-up weapons. Crafting ammo also consumes a copious amount of resources, and you can only progress as fast as your forges smelt iron.
Overall, in its current state, I'm iffy on recommending it, but it is free-to-play, so there's nothing to lose should you be interested in a Battle Royale game with dinosaurs.
