Ryse: Son of Rome had me entertained, for 5-6 hours.
This was the time it took me, incl. some idling, to complete the campaign, play gladiator a little, and realize that I found few reasons to go online.
This will be a short section. The game is gorgeous.
Scenery and music entwine to create a wonderful world.
Voice and animations realistic and highly believeable.
Ancient Rome with politics, men and others to polute it.
Not breathtaking, but engaging and very well done. Solid story and well above many others.
Well worth the 5-6 hours it took to consume.
You'll be walking along a fixed path and have fights of various sizes in designated areas. You won't be bored walking around though. Short distances, plenty of action, and things to fill your walks.
Nothing new brought to the scene here, except I find it dificult to remember the last time I found myself hiding in a cohort, shileded from the enemies flaming arrows as I attempt to advance and return fire.
Smaller tactical decisions here and there letting you decide in a few settings how you'd like to fight.
But all in all it's down to you and the way in which you handle a fight. You'll encounter a few different mobs (6 or so), which you'll quickly learn to handle, and a few boss fights.
There will be plenty of Quick-Time Events (QTE), druing fights, which (granted you succed) will give you a temporary advantage.
The game left me a bit unchallanged. Played on hardest setting possible from the start. It allows for a legendary setting as well (after 1st playtrough), but that will wait for another time, should I chose to experience the story again.
I used keyboard and mouse.
Controls very plenty fine. A minor issue with the use button from time to time, but really of little to no consequence.
I found myself missing a few hits on inanimate objects, but not once did I have control issues fighting.
Fighting similar to Assasins Creed and Batman Arkham, blocking and retaliating. Forcing an advance and countering.
A good concept I felt played well in this game.
Mind you if you are completely colourblind you might have an issue as the game guide QTE with colours, although you'll be able to pick up on other pointers with a little trial and error.
I recommend this game for its story, scenery and overall enjoyment.
But beware! It's a short game. I was glad I bought it on sale.

In case you couldn't tell,Ryse is set in the Roman era and this means you will be taking part in some enormous battles with some crazy set pieces.What possibly could make battles such as those more epic? Good Music. The soundtrack in Ryse is astounding as it fits unimaginably well with the setting and the overall feeling of the game itself. You'll be wading through barbarian corpses with an epic drum beat in the background and you can't help but feel like the ultimate badass.Again,the best part of the soundtrack is how it fits perfectly with the game itself and that seems to be something a lot of games tend to forget about these days.
Ryse is one of the best looking games that I have ever seen.From the great Roman colliseum all the way to the swamps near the edge of the world these environments are unbelievably breathtaking.The environments themselves are all varied and have special enemies that fit within them.The game manages to be incredibly high-res on everything from some pot in an alley to the folds of the emperors robes and still run well. So even though this is a console port,in terms of graphics it was ported over perfectly and it seems even given some improvements.
Ryse is a 3rd person hack and slash where you can use different executions to gain bonuses like health,regaining focus,or temporary damage boosts. The execution moves are brutal and feel unexplainably satisfying.The game breaks up the brawling segments with other segments like throwing spears at archers,mounting a scorpio turret,or organizing your soldiers to make a defense plan.The Pila segments,however,are incredily frustrating and you end up trying to hit the key to bring up the spear but instead it takes forever and you end up getting hit and having to restart the process all over again.The scorpio segments are almost always a blast because you're typically using it to either kill specific targets or hold the line against an unwavering horde of barbarians.The segments where you get to organize your men are pretty cool too because they have different ways to go about them. The scenarios aren't too different,for example in one level you're defending a wall from barbarian siege towers and catapults. You can tell your archers to either focus on the catapults and you wont have to deal with fireballs raining on your head,or you can tell them to attack the siege towers and you will have to deal with ladders instead of towers full of barbarians.Everything about the gameplay makes you feel like an unstoppable murderous force of vengeance come to take it's revenge on all of those who have wronged you.
Ryse is such an amazing game but sadly it has to be one of the most underwhelming games for me in terms of length. There could have been so much more to it,more levels,more story,more epic battles and interesting twists. Yet,even on the 2nd hardest difficulty (You can't play the hardest until you beat the game) i beat the game in about 6 hours.Something that I believe factors in to the game length is how easy this game is. On my first playthrough,on the 2nd hardest difficulty,I managed to only die maybe 4 or so times.The game is still phenomenal but I believe that it could have been more if they would have made it longer.
In Ryse there are 4 boss battles with 2 of those being the same fight at different points in the story.The boss battles feel so cheap and quickly slapped together as each fight literally uses the same exact fighting style as one of the tougher enemies that you will find throughout the bosses level. For instance,in the Boudica fight she fights exactly as the other dual-wielding barbarians do and so she ends up being a complete faceroll fight as long as you paid attention.The bosses do feel like epic fights but it's sad that they feel so gutted at the same time.

GRAPHICS
The PC edition of METAL GEAR SOLID V: GROUND ZEROES is definitely the definitive version. The game looks beautiful on even the lowest settings, and it isn't too hard to run it on max. Mods are available to enhance the graphics and unlock the framerate.
GAMEPLAY
GROUND ZEROES is definitely the best action stealth game on the market. The controls are great and the gunplay proves the game as a worthy third-person shooter, if that's how you choose to play. Although the main mission (yes, mission, without an S. There's only one story mission in GROUND ZEROES.) is fairly short, (it took me 99 minutes to complete on my first playthrough) there are 6 side missions that are included in GROUND ZEROES. Each of these missions vary in terms of gameplay, weather, and objective.
MODDING
As mentioned above, there are mods available to unlock the framerate and disable the DoF. Modders are currently working on model editors, but you can currently modelswap very easily. For more information on that, check the community hub guides.
To wrap it all up, I'd have to say that METAL GEAR SOLID V: GROUND ZEROES is one of the best games to come out this year. You're missing out if you don't purchase it. For 20 dollars, it's a steal.

Stronghold Crusader came out mid 2002 after the succesful Stronghold in 2001. Stronghold Crusader is set in the Middle East during the crusades rather then Europe like the first one, hence the name Crusader. This is a real time stratergy game with the focus of killing the enemy Lord/s. Careful though as he will be very strong and can take over 10000 archer arrows! don't worry it is done on purpose so you can kill him at a range, so best to send 10 plus swords men at him.
If you played the Original like I did many moons ago there are changes in this HD edition and NONE! are bad. There are 8 more characters to verus, more resolution sizes and graphics has imporved. Everything else is the same as the original which is amazing!
So the Pro's:
- Personally the best out of all Strongholds
- Unique RTS that requires not only military stratergies but also civil (do you make them drunk and fed or starve and whip them?)
- Arabian units are an awesome edition giving alot more unit choice
- Fire implementation in the game is great, see random guys on fire turn a city into a flame ball (happens more often then you think), yes this is a pro!!
- Large campaign and a few side stories 'missions'
- Great to plan with mates (LAN or over the net)
- Replayability in custom maps or make your own which is easily shared to other pc's when trying to match make
- alot of challanging Lords to play
- Fun castle building and designing to fit all military and civil works in and around
Con's
- 400 unit pop count, may sound like alot but it isn't when you are trying to kill 7 Lord's at once
- The Large map for 8 Players can seem very small in most instances
- If AI Lords placed close together or near iron it is create holes or even block themsleves in starving their kingdom.
- No unit or building healing (can repair towers and that's it)
- Would be good to make AI even harder, they have Lords to difficulty but it would be good if you can adjust it more
- Most of the time units will not attack the enemy until they are either told or the enemy are already bashing their face in
- Enemy AI with their army can be very disorganized making them easy prey
Overall I love this edition of Stronghold Crusader HD, I will continue to use it and LAN with friends. If you want a LAN game to kill some time this is great for you! (better to vs your friends for more of a challange).

What's that? No 3D-graphics? Well, guess what... It doesn't need that to be good!
Here you are, starting only with some wood, stone and gold. You build - you recruit - you fight - you win (?). It's a simple concept and a lot of strategy games follow this direction. In fact, Stronghold Crusader isn't really complex, so the first sight might give you the impression of a boring city simulator... For me, there's something wonderful about this simplicity.
The goal is to be the very best like no one ever was. Kill the enemy's king and get your well-earned peace while you defend your own crown-wearing buddy. Of course they won't invite you into their castle, so you have to invite yourself. In order to blast away their walls and towers, there are different ways, like hammering every single brick off the wall or dig a tunnel underneath it. They won't like you to be that rude, so they put archers on towers to keep your men away and you'll have to get rid of them first somehow! Either you ruin the towers with catapults or invade with own archers and fight back.
This isn't what makes Stronghold Crusader so enjoyable. The true entertainment is the possibility to be a rotten ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ to them! Every inhabitant of the castle is a free-walking NPC which can be killed too. It is incredibly annoying when your enemy has posted some archers beneath your farms and keeps killing your farmers. Not only is it very time consuming to fight off those archers, but it's also very stressful for the castle's economy. Every killed farmer means a lost delivery of food, and without food your people will get very angry. Your people start to leave your castle when you keep being such a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and soon you will only have three peasants left.
If this is still too weak for you, you can step it up and use dirty tricks to wreck'em! If you manage to lit an enemy's building on fire, it will spread out drasticly, burning down every house 'n' human. This could lead to a total destruction of the castle, making them to start from the beginning. Fire is a great element of the game, because it can turn a lost-believed battle into a success.
Otherwise I'd say it's a classic RTS. Build, fight and succeed. There are  singleplayer campaigns, but the true enjoyment is the multiplayer with friends, because of the nasty actions possible. Sadly you'll have to fiddle around with IPs and networks in order to connect to each other. Because this game doesn't require alot performance, the connection is always stable (at least for me it always was) and free of laggs.
All I can say is that I've played this game for whole days years ago and I still enjoy this piece. The graphics may look very old and bad, but I think it only adds to the charisma the game shows.

Do you like Civ V?  Do you like RPGs?  Do you like beautiful graphics?  This game was made for you.  Endless Legend take gameplay that is very similar to Civ V and puts it into a fantasy setting.  You explore, find minor factions to take over, collect materials, fight, and Quest to become the best faction.  Each main faction has it's own goals, strengths, and weaknesses.  Unlike Civ which has so many characters and countries to pick from, each with slight differences, Endless Legend has 9 to 10 Factions (depending if you have the DLC or not) that are extremely different from each other.  For instance, you have a faction that can't use food, they have to grow buy money, and a faction that cannot be a diplimat to others, they can only consume them.  And then there is the questing, OH THE QUESTING, this is my personal favorite part.  Each faction has their own quest to follow, these quest help you grow and gain the upper hand.  The only bad thing I will say about Endless Legend is that it can be overwhelming.  There are so many options and so much detail that it becomes easy to forget minor things that might hurt you later.  Overall, a very fun, very good game.  Also, less buggy than Civ V.
Who needs sleep when you have Endless Legend?

It's about as complex as Simon Says, and while it did get repetitive quickly, I'm not going to pretend that I was too sophisticated to derive some pleasure from it for the five hours Ryse lasted. I'm not proud of it, but a childish, depraved part of me enjoyed the shiny graphics and dismemberment every time.
It's essentially the combat from the Batman Arkham and Assassin's Creed games, which means a strong reliance on counters and follow-up strikes. What makes those games so much better than Ryse is that they start with those core mechanics, but then slowly add new gadgets, enemies, and other wrinkles. They have open worlds where I could use that combat to accomplish a bigger goal. Ryse has none of that.

+ Executions are cinematic and fluid
+ Multiple, simulataneous executions are possible (and look great)
+ Visuals are absolutely jaw-dropping, and do well to showcase some truly spectacular set design
+ Voice-acting is top shelft; every major and supporting character was voiced expertly
+ Myriad unlockables scattered throughout
+ Combat is superb and feels very polished
+ Writing for dialogue is very well-done, and complemented the voicing talent so well as to fit like a glove
+ Facial animations so well done they will leave the player totally floored; seemingly every nuance of twitches, quivers, and muscle movements are captured
- Moving in formation and giving orders during battles do little to affect the events that unfold, and the entire experience is largely dumbed down for the player's convenience; all choices are essentially hollow padding
- Precious little mob variation; there doesn't seem to be more than 8 or 9 enemy models throughout the entire campaign
- Historically, the game is not only inaccurate, it is entirely nonsensical; the writers essentially took all the famous names they could find in Roman history and plastered them on fabricated characters, many of them jarringly stereotypical
- Executions, which rely heavily on Quick Time Events (QTE) follow through and succeed even if the player fails the QTE; this is blatant hand-holding in the extreme, and does absolutely nothing to challenge the player
- Little is done to spruce up the combat throughout the campaign, and it therefore ends up feeling dull and repetitive by the game's conclusion
- Short campaign; I clocked in at just under 6 hours for a full playthrough
- Massive over-reliance on QTE; makes the entire game and playable combat feel scripted and low-effort

I beat Hocus Pocus back when I was a kid, and let me tell you: it was a pretty satisfying experience back then.  However, does the game hold up to current day?
Pros:
-Brilliant writing from Tom Hall, the man behind Commander Keen, Wolfenstein 3D, Rise of the Triad, and Anachronox
-Simple gameplay that is easy to grasp
-Fantastic pixel art graphics with interesting environements and monsters
-Four episodes with distinct end goals
-Some great retro PC music
-Interesting boss fights
-Lots of in-level secrets
Cons:
-Movement in general is somewhat jerky and jumping takes a while to get used to
-There are only really 5 types of enemies: projectile enemy, charging enemy, flying enemy, flying downward projectile enemy, flying sideways projectile enemy.  The rest are all reskins of one of the above
-Occasionally reused level tilesets are letdowns
-While simple, the gameplay becomes tiresome if taken in large doses- can become repetative!
-Switch puzzles are lazily designed and are only defeated by trial and error busy work
After revisiting the old classic, do I still find it to be up to par with how I originally felt about it?
Half and half.  The game's repetitive nature betrays it more in the modern day than it had previously, but the interesting environments, witty writing, and gameplay that I just generally find to be fairly fun, possibly out of nostalgia.  Without the tilesets and interesting monster designs it is entirely possible that I wouldn't give this game the time of day; however, as it is I would recommend this game given that you're a fan of DOS platformers.

So I am very very late to the 4X genre. I've seen people play Civ V, but not for any meaningful length of time, really, so my review is either worthless for anyone that knows the genre, or pretty helpful to the casual oberver that likes the name and/or art style and/or idea of the game. First off, I admit that my play time is NOTHING, and I haven't finished a game yet, though I do have a bit of experience with each of the major factions, and I think I grasp the basics enough to write a review for those people out there like me that want to play and enjoy this game. Hopefully I do a good job of curbing expectations and telling you what this game is in the simplest terms, because those are all I know. This will be a very stream of consciousness review that I HOPE is readable and helpful... Anyway, to start. this game is NOT Age of Empires like I thought. It's slower paced, and you don't have to fire a single arrow if you don't want to. Diplomacy is pretty fun, and I like exploring the map and just expanding my city and doing the quests you get in hidden ruins. Oh, yes, and there are quests in this game. And loot, and gear for your units, and your heroes have their own upgrade tree, which adds depth to everything. Combat itself works like a tactics game, in that when you come across another army or random monster group, you split off into two groups and move turn by turn on a grid, attacking and all that like  a simplified tactics game. I'm not sure if the units have special abilities yet, but if not that's fine, otherwise battles may take too long. They're fine as it is, lengthwise. The tutorial is daunting and a little confusing, which is too bad, because at first I didn't think I liked this game after I played it. A friend told me to watch a couple YouTube videos, though, by people that know the game, and I did, and it made more sense, and I picked it back up, so do that. Also, read the manual after the videos. I can't really think of anything else to say so far, other than if you're thinking you may like this game, you will. It just might take a bit more doing that some.

This and Fallen Enchantress Legendary Heroes are the fantasy 4x games of my dreams. FE:LH is both easier to get into and deeper, but also far more random and easier to break. EL has some strange city development ideas that I don't agree with (burroughs and their use of a city "level up" mechanic are a bad idea, I said it) but once you learn it you can work around it. Aside from that, you have hero units, you can assign them to a town or an army, they and their armies can level up.
A first word of warning: build burroughs OFTEN. And EARLY. Yes burroughs reduce the happiness of your people by 10 for each built in a city, but they also increase your yield of Food, Industry, Dust, Science, and maybe Influence, in a way that is often more useful and tangible than real buildings early on. Always make sure your city is at happy or better as there are severe economic drawbacks to having people at content or lower. Whether or not you decide to stretch your burroughs to reach for a tile with the FIDSI you're looking for, or to use attached "districts" to "level up" whatever they are attached to is usually a game of "how much happiness can I afford to lose?" which early game, is not much.
Often I would hover over something and see something in the tooltip that popped up that I wanted to know more about, but couldn't. There's an item that gives guardians less of a cooldown on their skills, but it calls it "army action cooldown" instead. One of your opponents will suddenly light up some dust towers in the world and you're told they're getting close to some kind of victory, but no clue is given to the player as to how to stop or prevent their winning, nor what victory condition it is. There's no preview for you to see which unit might be able to do what amount of damage to what other unit when moving or placing them on the battlefield, but it's all there clear as day during the actual attack. What does leveling up units actually do? How do I tell what the next unit level up will give that unit? There's a lot of information missing in this game that would make it easier to play.
Also forget the sick nidya quest, it is the worst one in the game, no matter when you encounter it; too many steps for a too-often bad reward, usually a technology you would have researched in 3 turns anyway. What a waste of time.
All that said, I do like this game. It's not finished yet, and time will tell if they ever do, but I would definitely recommend it to those who don't need/want to know all the information required to play this on a very challenging setting without a near-obsessive amount of inside baseball knowledge that the game never tells you.
I'm still having fun with it as of this review.
EDIT: 8 months later, still enjoying it, and updating my review for this purpose. I don't know what the problems all the other people are having are about, nor do I care. I play this game single player, with mods, and custom factions. I have never had any interest in playing a turn-based 4x game with other players. Aside from the recently introduced utterly broken diplomacy, it's still the same beautiful game it always was, for better or worse depending on how you look at it.

I can not believe this game is still recieving updates. I have the original store bought versions of Space Rangers 1 and 2, I think I got them back in 07 or 08. And the game is now in the best shape it has ever been. Regualery updated and new content shows up every so often.
Its immersive and expansive and can be severely difficult if you choose it to be so. Space Rangers HD is just.... Unique. You will not find another game like this anywhere, nor, will you find one as well maintained.

Do you like mystery/thriller games?
Hold on...let me rephrase that.
Do you like
mystery/thriller games?
At its core that is what Only If is. However, instead of being something along the lines of Amnesia in terms of being difficult and still a good game, Only If derives its difficulty from simply not being polished or clear about what to do. While part of this can be put off as adding into the mystery aspect and making the player figure out the puzzles in each level, but a couple of the levels are simply ridiculous to try and figure out without the help of a walkhrough. In addition, some of the platforming aspects of the game are slightly frustrating simply due to confusing level design such as having to jump on parts of platforms that simply look like aesthetics.
However, even with these problems, I still would recommend this game because of the experience that it provides. The story line is interesting (albiet difficult to follow at times) and really adds to the game as a whole. And even though I have pretty much bashed the gameplay, it does have its moments that makes it fun to play overall. On top of the whole thing, the achievements are all pretty simple to get and can help you improve your 100% complete rate on your profile if you are looking for that.
Overall, I recommend this game to people that don't mind less polished games with a few annoying parts and a ridiculous amount of swearing in relation to how short the game is. This game is pretty simple to complete and will probably take the majority of people somewhere around an hour or two to complete with all achievements (if you look up how to do them, since I am almost certain that you won't be getting the "One Day" secret achievement by accident).
Need a better reason? It's free and not a pile of garbage like a good deal of other free games on Steam.

Review Posted 18/11/2015.
A few things that should be noted if you are undecided about "purchasing" this game:
Its free, It's rated 18 plus & I should run on a fairly basic system.
If you get any entainment out of this then you are getting excellent value for noney.
In practice there is a picture in the first room that depending on where you live could be rated somewhere between "Its a cartoon character, thats a non event" to "that woman is barely dressed, that offends me greatly". There is a decent amount of swearing in the chatter between the player character and the non player character who communicates via a radio normaly located somewhere in the current room - It looks like the games icon. The third part of the 18 rating is its implyed that the character you are controlling is under the influnce of a mind altering drug. I have seen only one ending which is not very family friendly however nothing is shown, only discussed. From what I have read there may be a second ending which I have not seen so I cannot comment on that.
On the subject of a gaming system, realisticly I would expect anything with high end dual core, 2gb Ram & A dedicated video card sould be able to run it - well below what a standard gaming system has there days - the enviroments are fairly small and have minimal animated objects. If you have to have what might be thought of as an average system (Based on what an unspecialised store might try to sell you) Quad Core, 4Gb Ram & A dedicatd video card then it should run better of worse depending on if you know how to optimise your system. A computer system built with the intention of gameplay - High end quad core or better, 8Gb Ram or better, Mid to high end video card from the last few years will have minimal to no problems running this
The puzzles are fairly simple for the most part - If you find a puzzle difficult keep in mind the game is paying attention you what you type on your keyboard, along the lines of some of the older computer games that responded to typed commands. For example if you are asked where an item typing "to the right" might be a solution or standing in an logical location and trying a single word answer if that doesn't work. (no I'm not giving away the solution to two of the games puzzles here - Use a guide if needed)
If you happen to be a player that likes to speed run games the following controls might be useful to you:
Movement: WASD
Sprint: Shift (Sprint appears to be unlimited)
Jump: Space
Activate: E
Special: QWERTY section of your keyboard (The letters)
Shoot: Left Mouse Button (You will ony be shooting inanimate objects)
The game sould take somewhere between 15 Mins to an Hour to complete - if you know what you are doing.
The Size of the game is about 600 Mb which may download faster then it takes to finish it.

I didn't play Football Manager 2016, so many of the complaints I've seen others make about it lacking change since then are not things I have noticed. Last game that I played was Football Manager 2015.
It's Football Manager, so it is always going to follow the same basic format, the usual tried and tested features and layout are back. The interface and some of it's functionality has improved since FM15, there were annoying bugs, particularly with things like setting custom view profiles causing columns to disappear and refuse to display and almost all players being completely unrealisitc with their demans of game time(a first team player being in 70% of matches and yet screaming that he doesn't get enough match starts for example). There were numerous other little buggy annoyances that plagued the game but are too small to merit going into.
I am only 28 hours in with FM17 but I can gladly report that the majoirty of interface bugs seem to be removed, though when mousing over the information icon of a player the tooltip that pops up will still sometimes bug and stay there until you click the same icon again and move away from it; a bug that has been in every recent version I have played(FM 13, 14, 15).
The players also do seem to be less whiny so far, when they do whine they are much more reasonable. The key and first team players that I've had complain so far were happy as long as they started in ~50% of the matches during the promise interval and most seem content not to complain so long as I give them at least that many starts. I've not had any rotation/backup players complain yet.
All in all the game so far seems to be a good version of the series and less buggy than the previous versions I've tried. Still what people have commented on is true, it's not going to be radically different and blow you away; it's a Football Management sim afterall they can only innovate so much. The AI of opposition managers could still do with improving as it does still seem easy to get on long winning streaks as long as you have a strong tactic and aren't vastly out-skilled with opposition players; the majority of AI managers don't seem to use anything resembling complex tactics.

I stepped into this one, just expecting a pretty engine. But Ground Zeroes holds up in every aspect, from charecter design down to the little easter eggs. Everything has been so well thought out. Seaking into a military base at night.. in the rain, already seems fairly daunting, but the amount of options to play the game, the way you want is just immense. 11/10

The length of the main story for me personally (keeping in mind I didn't explore or go for max-completion) took a measly two hours to complete (which has sparked a lot of controversy). Despite this however, the story in Ground Zeroes is a very strong one, especially considering that the game was designed to inform fans of  the events that occurred before Phantom Pain.
A story in a Video Game or Movie however, is only as great as it is visually portrayed, Thankfully, the game looks beautiful. Kojima's previous installment to the series "Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns of Patriots" was a big step in visuals for its time. In fact, most Metal Games exceed expectations in terms of visuals.  Ground Zeroes is no exception. It has surpassed the visuals of Guns of Patriots by a long shot. The environment, the structures and the other soldiers look incredible.  If you haven't already,  simply watch the first cinematic on Youtube. It doesn't give away too much, but rather gives a small introduction as to what you will be required to do for the mission.  What you see in the first cinematic is a strong representation as to what you can expect from this game in terms of visuals. You will not be let down.
Sound quality is also something that you will be amazed by. Most objects/actions you hear is very accurate in comparision to its real world counterpart.
Due to the small length of the game, many will argue it is difficult for the player to grow attached to any of the characters at this point in time which I do agree with to some extent. That is something you will have to judge yourself IF you do decide to purchase this game.
Another thing to note is that I strongly believe this game appeals towards fans who have played previous installments as opposed to those who begin on this game. It does touch on events and reference Metal Gear Solid 3: Snake Eater and Metal Gear Solid: Peace Walker which may confuse some players. The game does give a very brief summary of the events that occurred in these titles but one may argue it's not enough.  If you have never played a Metal Gear Solid game do not start on this game. A HD collection was recently released containing both Snake Eater AND Peace Walker along with another popular title. Do yourself a favor and purchase it.
Whilst the stealth aspects of this game are great and work incredibly well, veterans will be disappointed to find the lack of new creative methods of concealing yourself. Bushes and shrubs similar to those from Snake Eater were my best friend throughout the story along with the tranq gun. However, I (personally) couldn't find nothing more than that. I may of missed it, but it certainly was not a prominent feature (feel free to correct me if I'm wrong).
The game does include "spec-ops" missions that attempt to extend the overall game time. I personally have not played them at this point in time but do intend on doing so.
To summaries, if your interested a beautifully presented stealth (which means not "runnin' and gunnin") title WHICH is not too long, Metal Gear Solid V: Ground Zeroes will certainly not disappoint.
-BEAUTIFUL VISUALS
-FREE OF GAME BREAKING BUGS
-SOUND QUALITY IS FANTASTIC
-STEALTH MECHANICS...HOWEVER (SEE CON POINT 2)
-DRAMATIC AND EXCITING STORY
-TIME TO COMPLETE MAIN STORY IS SMALL
-LACKING IN HIDING SPOTS
-MANY ARGUE IT'S TOO EXPENSIVE
-NEWCOMERS MAY NOT UNDERSTAND SOME REFERENCES TO THE EXPECTED EXTENT.
Final rating: 4/5.

Warhammer 40,000: Space Wolf:
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

The Word Bearers Space Marine Legion was one of the nine founding Legions who betrayed the Emperor of Mankind. On our last report, the Chaos Space Marine Legion successfully ambushed the strike cruiser of the Space Wolf squad on the orbit of the planet Kanak, forcing them to activate an emergency landing! Thankfully, their leader, Valgard Twice Slain, is still alive but needs your full tactical knowledge to help him and his squad to survive and lead them to victory on Kanak!
Warhammer 40,000: Space Wolf is a turn-based strategy game set in the Warhammer 40K world where you take command of the Space Wolf against the Chaos Space Marine Legion, The Word Bearers.
This game is currently an early access version and after launching the game your will arrive straight at the menu page. From here, you can select to play in Campaign mode or Multiplayer (PVP); there is also a Challenge mode, but it’s not available in this current build. You can click on the Armory within the main menu to look at the card deck for each of the classes. Here, you can forge new cards (you need points to create a card), from simple to extreme. Simple ones will cost substantially less than the extreme cards and are not as effective in combat in terms of damage. You can also fuse two of the same cards to upgrade it to another level. One thing you need to remember is that you only have thirty cards per deck and you must have a full deck to start a campaign or a PVP multiplayer game. Fusing too many cards might lead you to not having a full deck of cards. In terms of card descriptions, there is movement, health and weapons, as well as equip cards. Two equip cards can be placed on your hero and each of your soldiers when they appear in battle.

If you choose to start a campaign, the Power Armor class is automatically assigned to your leader. The Scout and Terminator classes will become available soon afterwards. I must say that you might find the missions quite challenging from the start. Remember, you might have a deck of thirty cards but only six are displayed per turn and they are totally random. It can become very challenging and frustrating but adds great re-playability to this game. You have two actions per turn and if you have an equip card in your first set, use it (equip) on your hero.  These cards will usually be triggered when a new enemy comes into your hero sight and will not cost you action points or inflict great damage. However, you have limited ammunition per card. As you progress into missions, your hero will be hit plenty of times. He has a rage gauge and each time he is hit the rage gauge will increase until it reaches the top. Then he will unleash a devastating attack upon a specific enemy. That also depends how quickly you can click your mouse button. To beat a mission, make sure you accomplish your primary objective(s). If Valgard dies, you restart the mission.
Graphically the game looks good and runs well. This is a challenging game, to say the least, and it might take you four to six goes per mission to beat it. It really depends which set of cards you get at the start and which ones you use during the mission. One thing I find odd is that your enemy can use a melee weapon diagonally, but you need to be in front of them to use yours!
I am really looking forward to the full version - I think this is going to be a cracker of a game.
Positives:
~~~~~~~
-	Nice graphics
-	Plenty of cards – forge new cards or fuse existing ones
-	Fun to play and challenging
-	Warhammer 40k world
-	Easy to find an online game
-	Achievements and trading cards
Negatives:
~~~~~~~~
-	Can be frustrating – maybe too much on the hardcore side of the equation
-	Can’t use a melee weapon diagonally but the enemy can
This version of Warhammer 40k: Space Wolf is impressive and I can’t wait to play the full version!

If you played through the gaming age so far, you'll more than likely like this game.  It's a mixture of Zelda new and old, and the entire Final Phantasy series.  Even a little bit of Ys.  Evoland includes a small bit of everything in the RPG series from NES to playstation 2.  It even includes a little bit of the hardware side in way of virtual hardware upgrades (ie. better graphics, better dvd drives, upgraded soundcards...)  Evoland is a overall decent game well worth a it's short play through time.
Combat wise you start in a top down Zelda/Ys style gameplay, hacking and slashing mobs away.  You then transition into Final Fantasy style combat (turnbased with similar menus) and then into newer age Zelda gameplay.  It's very fluid in doing so as well.
Graphics slowly upgrade throughout the game from simple 8 bit, to 16 bit, to 32 bit 2D, to 32 bit 2.5d (prerendered backdrops), and lastly to 32 bit full 3d.  It transitions fluidly and even lets you head back into previous areas to experience them in their updated new age qualities.
The game is rather enjoyable, being someone who's played through the original games it's mimicking.  My younger sibling who hasn't played much any of them didn't enjoy it however.  No word on their review though.  However, being that I've enjoyed it, you can expect 3-5 hours of gameplay out of it, more if you want to get all the achievements and items.
If you've played the games it mimics, I highly recommend picking it up on sale, if not outright.
If you played and liked various games like FF, Zelda, Diablo and others during the 80's & 90's... try Evoland, you should enjoy it!

This game sees you play as Marius a Roman officer as he sets off to Brittania with the XIV Legion to avenge the death of his family. Gameplay comes in the form off third person combat through linear levels featuring big set pieces.
Good points:
- I love Roman history and i loved the fact that this game lets you play a Roman soldier in combat. We mainly see Rome in startegy games so its refreshing in that sense
- The game looks great with some great graphics.
Bad points:
- The combat gets boring after a while. It just breaks down to you being put up against waves of enemies. You defeat one group, move on then fight another with the occasional set piece to break it up.
- If you hate QTE then you'll hate this game because it's crammed with them. QTEs performing executions in combat, QTEs during interactive sequences it's endless.
- The games main campaign is short. Really short. There's multiplayer which i tried briefly where you co-op with one other player to defeat enemies in an arena. It's ok but not good enough to keep me hooked.
- This game is also pretty buggy and glitch. 4 times i had to exit the game because of glitches and bugs. Once an enemy i had to kill glitched through the ground, another time the game wouldnt respond to the combat buttons being pressed. It's ridiculous for whats supposed to be a AAA game.
Overall i cant recommend this. I love the games Roman setting putting you in the sandals of a Roman soldier on the frontline , and i hope this is a setting more developers might explore for new games. But the glitches, repetitive combat and constant QTE's ruin the experience.

First off--It says I only have like an hour on record, but I have actually played much more of this. I've had to uninstall it once or twice and gotten a new computer once, so at some point in all that it cut away the record.
Victoria II is a fantastic game with some deep (but not unfixable) flaws. It delivers on its promise of great power politics and geopolitical tensions, and captures a Victorian spirit to boot. Trying to bring the great powers off the cliff of war is a ton of fun, and once you slide over that cliff mobilizing your reserves and fighting for the future of Europe is a great experience.
However, there are a couple of major problems that don't break the game but severely reduce its fun:
+Political system: stupid, meaningless, repetitve events about which economic policy you support every time there's an election. While the party system is well done and the parties even shift their policies over time to fit new political situations, your ability to impact the electoral system is alternatively meaningless (ie, the take-a-stand-on-this-issue events) or so hamfisted as to be unbelievable (ie, set a national focus to "increase party loyalty to x party" in your most populous state, and 0 context-giving events and decisions sparked by this later the people magically support your party.)
+The opaque world market trading system, and the ridiculous overflow of meaningless information about literally every individual citizen in your state. The trading system is not easy to navigate, nor is it clear why it should even be an option since you can play the game completely successfully without once investigating that system. The same applies for the overflow of information about EVERY person in your empire and whether they had bread or something better for lunch today (ie, "daily needs fulfillled" versus "life needs," etc etc). Add to this overflow of information that there is no easy or intuitive way to make use of it in any way, and you have a recipie for another redundant mechanic that makes you wonder if you're missing something or if the game itself is.
+Micromanagement--specifically, of your sphere of influence as a great power (try playing as Austria and you'll find that most of your first 20 years in game are turning "influence" levels up or down a notch on various German minor states to compete with Prussia) and of the individual citizens of the empire (how many capitalists do I have, how many officers, etc etc etc.) Nothing wrong with managing your diplomatic efforts or trying to channel which careers are favored in your society--in fact, those are critical for a game like this--but the way they are being done is not good.
+Things clearly missing. Namely, a WWI and/or WWII bookmark scenario. The game runs from 1836-1945 or so, and has a great power system that really captures the pre-WWI mentality of policymakers in Europe--yet there is no scenario for this. Secondly, there are some good events and decisions throughout the game, but even for major powers like Austria or Britain you get the sense that its unfinished (not enough actual decisions or events, particularly in mid to late game.) Additionally, few of these events are anything but scripted and as such very often do not comport with whatever reality you are actually facing at that moment in the world.
Despite all these problems, this game accomplishes its primary objectives admirably. There is a great and fun colonization system, a well-made tech tree system, excellent mechanics for great power conflict or conflict resolution, excellent representations of political parties and movements of the time (ie, the spectre of communism over Europe is all too real) and a generally well-done "Victorian" feel.
I know Paradox will never update this game again, but I really hope they make a Victoria III and take some of these issues into account.

This plays out a lot like Europa Universalis and a bit less like Crusader Kings or Stellaris, but all are essentially the same excellent strategy game at heart. I had been a little put off by the more modern focus and then by the glitchy tutorial and all of the complexity surrounding the different population types and trade goods. It turns out that I didn't have much to worry about.
It's good enough to know that producing more gets you more money and to let the AI work out the exact trades as needed, as is set by default. It's also just good enough to know that giving money or tax breaks to certain groups gets you more of them (soldiers in particular are useful) or that putting a focus to generating more of a particular profession will get you what you need.
Being able to play as America is a fun change of place from the more European centric games in the Paradox portfolio, and giving one options to mirror historical events is a lot of fun. Absorbing Texas and working towards the same in Hawaii while grabbing territory from Mexico is fun. Attempting to avert the civil war (or worse, letting the north secede) is also a lot of fun.
I particularly like being able to use political sway on other nations to draw them into your sphere of influence, which gets you relationship and trade benefits with them. The eight great powers of the world is a fun dynamic as well, particularly when they get called in to vote on disputes in hopes of avoiding armed conflict after say, competing over the same colonization territory with another nation.
Research is also more engaging in this game, as it allows certain country specific policy options and many techs can kick off a monthly small chance to spur on inventions, which provide a host of smaller upgrades to your nation.
The interface is confusing and takes a little while to work through as with any Paradox game, but despite being a few years older at this point, this is still a well worthwile game.
Edit: I will add that as the game (appropriately) sends retribution after you for being too aggressive, it can get a little boring/passive at times when you run out of territory to take that you have a right to take. It can be a good, calm experience at that point, but eventually you kind of run out of legitimate things to do.

SR:AWA fixes a few things, adds higher-res, and adds a lot more stuff.
Stuff? What stuff? That is what I always wanted to know.
But no one ever would say. They'd be like "they added a few things".
OK, like what?
WHAT?
Not even the game developers explain all that they have added.
SO HERE IS THE JIST OF IT:
-You can join the Pirates FOR REAL.  Before, you would be a pirate by ACTING like a pirate. You can be a good guy or bad guy and land at their bases. They didn't care. NOW, you can still do that, but now you can OFFICIALLY join them.
So you are a Ranger but you can join the Pirates. To advance, you have to ACT like a pirate, earning pirate "points" for doing various nefarious things (attack transports, get them to give-up cargo, extort money from them, or blow them up, etc.).
-In the Pirate faction, there is a "rank" system, like the Rangers have. Once you earn enough pirate points to reach the next rank, they don't just give it to you. Rather, you will be given a quest to complete. This can be a frustrating chore. Given Pirates are "take no kraaap!" types, you have to take it from them to complete a quest to "rank-up". One quest, I had to land on a planet and do something, but since I'm a pirate, and the planet hates me, I get captured right away and they try to throw me in jail. LOL. The only way out is to pay $$$$$ in fine (racks up as you raid/destroy ships to rank-up in the Pirate faction) or destroy a bucket-load of Dominators (who are they? Imagine if Skynet from Terminator built spaceships to conquer the galaxy). SO, what are really "non-pirate" activities, that must be completed, really make the Pirate-rank-progression thing a real buzz-kill.
-Destroy stations. The Dominators in the other games could do it. Why couldn't you? NOW YOU CAN. So when you go "full-Pirate-aggro" in the past games, all civilian ships, military ships, and some Rangers are hostile to you, and you can battle them to all you want to blow them out of the stars.
Now you can blow all their precious space stations out of the stars too.
I always wanted that in the game. Stations always have a huge impact on a star system, and the ability to drastically alter a system, So are you♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥at the Rangers? The Military? Scientists? Medical? Business Centers? Etc. BLOW THEM UP. You can take out any station now.
(Maybe next they should add planets? lol.)
-New ships models/types, new weapons, new devices/ship-parts. This is the best. SR2:Reboot always needed MORE stuff. More gear is better. You always reached a point where you're like "This is all?" and hoped there'd be mods or something that added new stuff. The game could seriously benefit from a Diablo/Drox Operative-type loot system, in my opinion. They developers tried to expand on this as best they could without ruining the game. They split up ship's abilities into Energy, Shield, and some other thing. Unfortunately, it's never really explained, you have to go online to figure out what "E:" "S:" and stuff means. Pretty stupid. But it's not imporant. What you look at is the item description and what it will do for you and your ship. "This weap will do 10-20dmg and has range of 300". That's pretty much all I need to know.
A bunch of fans of the game are REALLY♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off at the new changes to items/weapons.
I'm sure they had a "routine", to start-up, progress, and which ships/items to go for, with each game they play (or just used to same game. On SR2:Reboot, I've been playing the same character/game for like 4 years. lol.).
SO, the developers coming in and changing things, "messes up" the routine.
Overall, I didn't find it that drastic or distracting. It did seem to make progressing a bit harder, and drawn out.
The game is a "long game" in that sense anyways.
-New ships for Dominators too. I like have they might have a command/flagship in their fleets now sometimes.
-New songs (not too many though)
-High-Res available, and new graphics/effects. There are new combat-FX which look better than SR2/SR2:Reboot. Not THAT much, but it's more fluid and more tight. A very welcomed change. As for the HD/High-Res....FORGET IT. While the game runs great maxxed-out, everything looks too small anyways. Like watching beetles zap each other all over the screen. NAH, I'd rather be able to actually see the ships closer than this, and not with a magnifying glass. You can adjust the font but it looks stupid when playing at max res and each letter is the size of an ant's behind.
Still, if you have a really humungous monitor, it would be better suited. Even with lower-resolution settings, the game looks great. It always did before so why should it not?
It seems the whole "high-res" just really serves to make everything "smaller".
It doesn't appear to me that they tightened the graphics at all, but rather, made it to where you're more "zoomed out" and slapped "HD" on it.
Seriously, if you play on highest SR2:Reboot res, the game looks totally the same.
That's not a bad thing. Like I said, the "high-res", is really just the game more zoomed out and not suffering from graphical anomalies as best I can tell.
-I can't remember anything else that stood out as different. Tons of small improvements here and there, like stations do a better job shooting down asteroids passing by, that spawn more minerals.
-ONLY SERIOUSLY BAD THINGS: I hate that ships run away super-fast, if they are losing a battle. The game still has problems with "targeting". Like, you can't target anything outside your weapon range, but you can fly within range once the "turn-based/simulatenous-real-time" starts. So why not be able to set the ship to fire automatically at a designated target? If you use the default option to "attack target", the ship flies moronically.
Your ship will fly away from the enemy, because the enemy might be flying on a path to where doing that manuever will put your weapons in range.....BUT IT DOESN'T WORK HALF THE BLEEDING TIME.
In SR2:REBOOT, this happened, but it actually appeared to work effectively 75% or more of the time. Now, it'sl ike 40% of the time. That's REALLY frustrating.
OH YEAH, and while I appreciate that ships "realistically" try to flee and land somewhere to get away and repair, when this happens though, they have some sort of magicaly "turbo-boost", where they fly off at "cheat" speeds.
They land.
They know if you are camping them.
Once you fly far away, they will launch, and attack, or fly away.
So you play a ton more of "cat/mouse" in AWA. They ran away too in SR2:Reboot, but not with some super-turbo-boost like that. So it really ruins combat in the game, drags it out endlessly, in fact.
I seriously believe they need to release a patch that nerfs this.
OVERALL:
Personally, I'd want to recommend SR2:REBOOT instead.
That was the best of the SR series.
BUT...AWA streamlines the game and adds stuff, and despite its issues--they aren't much, so I'd have to go ahead and recommend SR:AWA. If you play SR2:REBOOT, and then play this new one, you'll be like "Dude, this has more stuff to do, more things? Why didn't you tell me? WHY?!"
Now you know! :D

For anyone on the fence about Space Rangers, if this doesn't sell you on the game I don't know what will. This is all just one single quest:
I'm playing a kind of scumbag ranger, smuggling contraband and generally being sleazy. At one point I took an escort mission, when the other ship and I were in deep space with no one around I opened fire on them until they surrendered and offered me credits to stop attacking them, which I accepted, I then flew to the originating base and told them I had successfully escorted the ship and got paid there as well - that kind of thing.
I'm flying around looking for opportunities and I see a big collection of ore and mineral, just floating around. I fill up my cargo bay and head to the nearest inhabited planet to unload my haul, but I wasn't really paying attention because I was an outlaw on this planet and the police caught me as soon as I landed. I was sent to prison where I was given the option of serving my sentence or attempting to escape. I chose to serve my sentence, and it turned in to a prison simulation where I had to survive 75 days in prison while balancing relationships with the prison officials and the other prisoners.
Luckily I'm fairly rich on the outside and access to my credits was not cut off in prison. I first ran in to an old prison veteran who gave me prison survival tips for a few credits each and he kept basically telling me that if I was going to be a "good boy" and suck up to the guards and be a model prisoner, the other inmates would grow to hate me. He also mentioned a cafeteria where I could get food which would make my life easier, but if I spent too much money at the cafeteria, the other inmates would start to get jealous.
Then I went to the Cafeteria and spent a lot of money to buy food for every inmate. This instantly bought me the respect of all of the prisoners, but the guards got suspicious and started keeping watch on me. On my way back to my cell I smuggled a fork and a spoon, but when I got back to my cell someone had raided my locker and stolen some credits. I figured I would need to beat someone up over this, so I went to the gym to get ripped, but dropped a barbell on my foot instead, so I had to go back to my cell, where some shady inmate wanted to sell me a tape recorder. I bought it without any idea why I would want it and went to bed.
The next day the prisoners were holding a fist-fight championship, so instead of going to work or the gym or the library, I went to the fight. When I got there I found out that the prison warden loved these fights and he was in attendance. I requested to become a participant in the hopes of gaining respect from both camps. The first fighter came out hard and strong and I was forced in to a defensive stance and couldn't get any hits off, the guy eventually pummeled me so hard within a few rounds that local newspapers were reporting on how I "took it in the face".
When I woke up, I decided to use my spoon to start digging a tunnel out of my cell. After a day of digging I had only made it 7m, so I gave up and regretted not working out at the gym instead. The next day I decided to play it straight and went to get a work assignment, but they wanted me to paint a f**king fence which is bullls**t so I refused. The guards beat the s**t out of my and threw me in solitary for the night. When they brought me back to my cell the next day, I was confronted by a group of inmates. See, when I first went in to prison and I bought respect from the inmates, they took a real liking to me, in fact they liked me to much that I was named "the prison Don", and they... disposed of the old Don. However, I was f**king up too much, now things were ruined, and they regretted escalating me to Don status. They brandished some shanks and metal pipes and pretty much told me I was dead unless I paid them off. I also had the option to fight, but between the fight I lost earlier and the beating I took from the guards, I figured it was a bad idea, so I paid them off.
I really wanted to go to the medical center, but today was another fight day and it was closed down - f**k. I went to the fights and decided to participate again, in my already weakened state. My opponent was a little scrappy guy but I guess he knew what he was doing, because he knocked me out, then picked me up and threw my body straight out of the ring, godd**nit. The papers made fun of me again and I went to bed.
I checked the calendar. I've only been in here for seven days, and I have another 68 until release.

Graphics / Visuals - The visuals are really nice and smooth, as long as you turn off ‘noise’ in the settings. Other than that, great visuals!

+ Difficult but fun

- Dead Multiplayer

Space Wolf is a turn-based collectible card game in which players will take the role of members of Space Wolves. It is a game that needs some work but has nice potential. You use a Card-based system to control the main characters’ combat actions and movements. You use cards to equipment, powers and skill your units to give you either move or neat attack skills.  Cards vary in rarity and maximum level (how many times players can upgrade the card). Cards can be leveled by combining two cards of the same type. Which I did not know. Players can create their own decks, picking the cards that fit their gameplay style and needs. There is a nice campaign mode to start, you can craft more cards. I have to say some good pros and cons
PROS
A: Graphics and Effects are pretty solid and nice character movement. Hero craft deserves some kudos for effort.
B: Like most TCGs, Hearthstone, Duelist, Warbands Bushido, another game  that mixes several games in one, card game, turn based tactical, and strategy, isometric and classic Warhammer 40k characters in one. If you like RTS or used to the fast paced 40k mmos, this is not for you.
C: What pulls you in here is not the storyline but the battle system. Trying to figure combinations, placement, and despite a tabletop warhammer classic, Does not count on dice AI or those mechanics to play. This has a great modern polished look to the classic early turn based Warhammer 40k games.
D: Game mechanics maybe be too simple for some, but a fun game to try of all ages. My kids enjoyed playing it.

Ryse turned out to be a good in-between game. I just came off of 150 hours or Witcher 3 and was looking for something short and quick. I didn't expect much from Ryse, but it actually delivered in some ways I didn't expect. The story was surprisingly engaging. I've always been interested in Roman history, so the setting was already right up my alley. It strays far from actual history, of course, but it hits enough of the right notes to satisfy. There are also some nicely realized characters with some decent voice acting. The main character, Marius, and the Briton princess, Boudica, are particularly good.
The combat is simple but fun. It is exceedingly gory, particulary the finishers, so if that's not your thing, you might want to steer clear. There is a fairly extensive upgrade system, but at least in the single-player campaign on medium difficulty, the upgrades don't make much of a difference. This isn't a difficult game. The combat is interspersed with turret sequences for variety, but they are mostly forgettable. My biggest complaint are the final few boss battles at the end of the game. The mechanics of these fights are pretty weak, basically boiling down to dodging boss attacks and hitting them--just once--when their backs are exposed, for very minimal damage, and then doing it again. And again. And again. These fights aren't hard, just boring. It's an unfortunate end to an otherwise fun game.

As an aging gamer living in a time where innovation moves as naturally as a river of bricks, Ground Zeroes, and by extension Metal Gear Solid 5 as a whole, has scratched an itch I never knew that I had.
Let us get this out of the way.  Yes, this game is small.  It has a mere seven missions which can all be completed within 10 minutes with the right technique, and is essentially a beta test for the fundamental gameplay of MGS 5.
The gameplay of Ground Zeroes is quite possibly the most enchanting and immersive I have ever witnessed.  The game is by no means realistic, as Snake can take quite a few bullets to the chest and then dig his head in the gravel to rejenerate his health, but it gives the player incredible control of the gameplay.  An example of this is the brilliantly designed extraction system.  In most(all) other "action" games, your point of extraction is pre-determined, as well as mostly every other really "awesome" moment.  In Ground Zeroes, I desparately threw three prisoners into the back of a truck as jets approached the prison base and drove them to the helicopter I had called in 30 seconds before.  I then unloaded the prisoners onto the helicopter, only to be assaulted by an armored car, which I promptly blew up by expelling a few rockets into it.  And finally I hopped onto the helicopter and shot at a lot of dudes who oddly enough never wear helmets before the mission was finally over.  The best part of these moments is the player is in complete control of the action.  In previous Metal Gear games, this would more than likely have been a cutscene, or at least a scripted event, yet I organically produced an awesome moment thanks to the incredibly open sandbox the FOX engine creates.
A quick note on the graphics.  I have always been an advocate of gameplay > graphics, but the astonishing graphics of this game are both pleasing to the eye as well as a function of the gameplay.  It would be awfully hard to interpret the light levels of different areas if the game looked any less brilliant.  So, in short, the game looks gorgeous for good reason.
As far as story is concerned, yes you should read the wiki or at least play Peace Walker if you want to understand it.  Fortunately, this Snake's story is significantly less convoluted than that of Solid Snake, so no time paradoxes here.  The removal of the hand-drawn cutscenes and the new voice of Snake(the excellent Kiefer Sutherland) do make me a bit sad, but they do not remove from the gameplay and I can understand why these decisions were made.  In short, any changes to the story and, more importantly, the presentation of that story are forgiveable.
In conclusion, this is an incredible game with some of the most interesting gameplay I have seen in a long history of games.  For once we can be the awesome action hero of our childish dreams, and we also get to be Kiefer Sutherland.

Victoria 2 is better than Europa in many ways. Please don't waste your money - Not even the offer price.. I did not enjoy playing this game! Because the game doesn't work - loads falling off the forklift for no reason etc..
-- I have a lot of experience with these types of vehicles both in real like and in other games like farming-simulator. So, I think I am well qualified to review this game.
--The first pallet truck in the store was OK, yet I was enourmously annoyed with the game makers, because they send you all the way back to the start if you fail. (I just moved onto the next vehicle I had unlocked).
--Its totally unreasonable to ask us to do all of those jobs again. just because you failed one time trial by 1 second. Yep. That was it for me.. I lost count of all the jobs I'd done, there were that many, so I guess I must have been somewhere near the end if there is an end to this game.  No-way am I doing all of that again..
Next - I hate the time trial aspect of games like this. it shows little imagination, when the only option they give you is time trial. If this is a 'simulator' the makers should know that speed is not the primary issue. Saefty is. I worked in a warehouse once. If pallets needed to be moved, a reasonable time would be given - Simple as that.. In this game, I failed because the game only gave me about 7 minutes to move three pallets from inside to outside in the car park.
-Plus I was already outside, (damn it). - failing by just one second and having to restart at the very begining. Nope - stupid useless game...
Then when I got onto the next vehicle; the forklift truck - (I know how to drive one in real life), I know about tilt and carrying the load low etc.. (I held a side lift licence for four years)!!!..  Yet - try lifting the load up to the shelf! It won't go . besides the load creeping forwards whilst you are driving - or not being able to get the pallet on the forks in the first place, the last straw is when you try to life at the destination.  As your forks go up- the load creeps off the the forks - This is impossible in Real Life. Basic angle and gravity dictate it.  The game is flawed and stupid..
Yet this Funking load still persists to creep further and further until it falls off the forks. Its a stupid fail - that should never happen.. This game is NOT WORKING for that reason..  Talk about broken. Now I know why it was only £1.74 I still feel robbed and let down at that.. But never mind - its only £1.74 - but the price isn't the point..
Now I know why all those other commentors were saying this is a pile of crap - (because it is). It would have been great - if it actually worked.. If the forks don't actually lift - then the game is a fail - isn't it?
Basically, I usually enjoy this type of game. My first thoughts when I read what other people were saying about this game, (all were negative), was that, perhaps people should have to pre-qualify themselves to be able to comment on a game like this, by having had played other similar games.
My thoughts are, that perhaps, the developers of any game should be able to set an experience level, attained (hours) playing other games that are similar to theirs..  Like I love Farming Simulator - yet people claim it is boring - but then they usually play COD or GTA5 - So sure - they are going to find it boring after playing fast paced games like that..
In a similar way - its why old farts who cannot play COD, BF and GTA5 should not be allowed to comment on them, because these multiplayer encounters are just too quick for them. But - my point is, that I do see peole my own age; who cannot play -  marking games like COD and BF down as crap.. I think its the same with this type of game.. Only opposite...  The younger people - who play the fast paced games like COD etc, will always shoot down games like this and games like farming simulator, Train Simulator, ETS2 etc..

First of all let me say, as of today i´m glad to have payed 10 bucks for this, just because the devs are that awesome. I found a game breaking issue where i produced a situation in which the game was not playable anymore (flaw in the crafting system), and it took LESS than 2 minutes from posting my issue over response from the devs to solving the issue for me.
Read todays patchnotes and you see, they seemlingly also put it into the fixes at the same day... That alone is worth 10 bucks in my eyes.
Now the game... I give it a yes, because it is a cool game... But be warned: if you are - just like me - a complete noob to this game, it is GODDAM hard... you NEED to be a guy who is willing to try a mission several times, has a natural resistance to frustration and doesn´t mind it if some situations go bad just by bad luck.
It is a card driven "table top" style strategy game and thus there is a huge random factor coming with the system. i´m personally hoping that there will happen alot of balance in that regard, or at least some kind of difficulty options over time. Nontheless, if you are in luck and get the right cards from your deck to your hand right away, it is great fun to smash the heretic´s skulls. This issue might also get better with owning more and more cards and being able to have less "useless" cards in the deck later, i will see and probably edit this review at some point.
It has the potential to belong to the better WH40k games out there, and i would say it already does.
Hardcore tactical guys will certainly ask me what i´m talking about with view on the difficulty, average to casual players will probably know what i mean... brain-lazy people should stay away from it though :)
All in all, i can see the devs love their game and it is done in a way that shows it. I recommend it, as well as an appointment at your anti-stress-therapist :)

Я добрался до игры с новым балансом оружия.
Ну что сказать, "война поменялась". Самое заметное нововведение - рукопашное оружие может атаковать несколько целей за раз, например, молотки или когти, а ещё им теперь можно атаковать цели по диагонали. Дистанционное оружие теперь зачастую не может бить по целям в упор (я считаю, что это правильно, ближе к Бэку - никто не стреляет из болтера влоб), поэтому нужно собирать колоду с учётом ситуаций, когда враг подбежал вплотную к нам. Игра обалденная!
Прежде всего, должен сказать, что это - порт мобильной игры. Но не тупо перенос, а полноценное переосмысление. Да, тут много общего: миссии, сюжет, карточная механика. Но здесь просто чумовая графика для такаой маленькой игры, новый баланс и никаких проклятых микротранзакций, ура! Это действительно круто, и благоадря этому стим-версия очень сильно отличается от мобилки в лучшую сторону.
SpaceWolf - это очень смесь коллекционной карточной игры с пошаговой стратегией, запралвенная таким хардкором, что х-ком забился в угол и нервно смолит самокруткой. По ощущениям очень похоже на режим "железный человек" из х-ком же. одна ошибка и неправильно выставленный персонаж получает тонну урона от противника. Комбинация системы усилий и пошаговости выглядит сперва очень сложно, но как только разберёшься в механике, то влюбляешься в неё. Предстаьте, как если бы ваш разведчик в х-ком делал не 1 действие, а несколько? И здесь это не только возможно, но и является обязательным для победы. Если упростить, то чем дешевле по усилиям стоит карточка, то тем раньше персонаж получит новый ход. Пример. у ближайших к нам противников по 10 усилий. Бьём их из огнемёта один раз и завершаем ход. Снова получаем ход, но у противников уже по 2 усилия. Расстреливаем их из болтеров - и вся наука.
И да, здесь действительно много и часто делают больно. Но мы не рискуем своими любимыми персонажами, которые умирают навсегда из-за одного промаха (ага, опять х-ком) - максимум, придётся перезапустить миссию, чтобы взять этот чёртов сундук и параллельно убить 15 врагов.
Игра определённо отрабатывает каждый вложенный рубль. А это только ЕА. Но уже сейчас игра выглядит и играется круче, чем большинство не AAA-игр по вселенной WarHammer 40000 за последние годы.
Я совершенно точно могу рекомендовать игру всем любителям тбс.
За Императора!
П.С. А, ещё тут крутые х-реи с хедшотами.
