I bought this on a whim yesterday, as I had a few pounds left in my steam wallet, so figured "hey why not". I've only played the first 3 missions, so bear that in mind while you read this review.
If you've ever played 40k, think "Kill team". You get dropped in a zone with one soldier, your charachter (by the way, don't let him die - if you do it's game over). After beating a few Word Bearers you get a couple of reinforcements, and can move on to completing your mission.
The first mission is unnecessarily difficult and long. You have to think very tactically to beat it, and there is an element of luck, it took me 4-5 tries. Mostly it involves figuring out how to bait the AI into splitting their fire, if they gang up on one of your troops, he's probably done for.
One tip I'd give is: don't be too quick to press forward. Try and clear the area of enemies first, because more will appear, and you can quickly find yourself overwhelmed. This isn't always possible though, so again, tactics.
May be a little slow paced for PC players, but I'm having a blast with it, and would recommend you give it a go. It's well worth the £8 I paid for it.

In this Game you will need to think about tactic, and gameplay can enthrall you for several hours without a break. Space Wolf has simple graphics, but beautiful style! I definetly recommend this game!

This is a Steam adaptation of a brilliant mobile game developed by Herocraft. The game natively supports a wide variaty of languages such as all major European ones, Russian and even three Asian languages, which is a huge plus.
For now 'Space Wolf' is in the Early Access stage, but you can already experience the addictive mechanics of tactical card combat, where you can equip some cards cards and use others to attack, activate a special ability or even just move, etc.
I've only played a couple of early campaign mission so far, and they are nothing like the ones in the mobile verison of the game. PC can handle much bigger and more complex maps with a bigger amount of enemies, so the game feels fresh even for the mobile version veterans.
There are three classes of characters available - spacemarines, terminators and scouts, each with a unique weapons and special abilities.
The graphics are nothing to write home about but look pretty solid and is able to depict a fierce battles of Space Wolves against Chaos space marines. Attention - when you first start the game graphics settings are set on low, make sure you turn it all the way up in the Settings menu.
I for one decided to back this interesting project and see where it is going, especially since the price is so low.
Это Steam-версия мобильной игры от русских разработчиков Herocraft из Калининграда, поэтому игра сразу поддерживает русский язык, а также все европейские и азиатские языки.
Пока "Space Wolf" в раннем доступе, но уже сейчас можно опробовать цепляющую механику тактических карточных боёв, где карты экипируются, используются для атаки, активации способности или просто передвижения и т.д.
Пока попробовал только первые миссии кампании и уже заметил, что они совершенно не такие, как в мобильной версии. Компьютер позволяет использовать большие и сложные арены с множеством врагов на экране одновременно.
Доступны три класса воинов - космодесантники, терминаторы и скауты, у всех разное вооружение и способности.
Графика звёзд с неба не хватает, но выглядит вполне неплохо и отлично передаёт картину жестоких сражений Космических Волков против космодесанта Хаоса. Внимание, при первом запуске игры стоит самая низкая графика, надо включить высокую графику в настройках.
Лично я принял решение поддержать многообещающий проект от наших разработчиков, тем более что цена вполне антикризисная.

What a past couple of years for 40k games, if it weren't in early access I'd say add this one to the scrapheap.
I assume the tutorial mission is unbeatable to hide the fact that the rest of the game isn't there yet. After my 3rd attempt to beat the first mission (average of 3-4 freezes and crashes per attempt), I've decided to let this one simmer in early access for a while before trying again.
The fact is, there is what seems to be a fun and well implimented card driven tactics game beneith the veneer of♥♥♥♥♥♥that's covering it up, which is the only reason why I am not simply refunding this. However it is worthy of note, there is Early Access and there is barely playable pre-alpha garbage, and right now this is the latter. DO NOT BUY unless you are willing to take a risk that the game will be good at some point, because it isn't now. Which is a shame.
I will update this review as development continues, as there is a lot of promise here, but there was a lot of promise in eternal crusade as well.

in short: grab it if you like multiplayer or really enjoy 40k universe; The multiplayer is really good and engaging (when you are fighting the enemy in somewhat similar conditions). If you are looking for a singleplayer experience - i'd skip it for now.
-	Fun to play
-	Actions taking time is a good approach: you can make two „long” actions and allow the enemy move before yours, or you can do a short one, take a break and attack again before the enemy gets a chance to move
-	The graphics are well polished
-	Plenty of cards/content to diversify your playing experience
-	Well, it’s warhammer 40k universe. Which is pretty badass by itself
-	Multiplayer is actually good
-	Some enemy units can attack you with melee attacks diagonally, but your melee attacks can only go in front
-	Very difficult (not sure if intentional) – in missions, enemies just keep spawning when you step on certain areas (meaning you can’t go around the enemy sometimes without spawning new ones). The difficulty did not bother me much, but this unpredictability is killing it.
-	Deckbuilding UI is clumsy and unintuitive. (But the early access roadmap promises to tune it)
-	Cannot turn your character without moving (which is essential for the gameplay, as you cannot shoot the enemies that stand on the side without wasting a move)
-	The game feels too reliant on RNG. 70-80% hitrate makes you feel screwed by the game quite often. If you are lucky to dodge enemy attacks – great. If you shoot 3 times in a row and miss – it stops being cool. Obstacles don’t do much and do not seem to impact the shooting.
Not surprisingly, I’m going to compare the game battle system to x-com. I’m going to talk about single player, because multiplayer do not have most of these issues (well, except for random factor).
Right now, the issue with the game is not the content. Personally, I did not enjoy the game due to unpredictability: the enemies just spawn in too big numbers in pre-scripted manner. X-com avoids it by showing fog of war: that way you can scroll around the map and at least try to take into account that an enemy can be hiding somewhere. In this case: the map is wide open, but the enemies simply appear in front of you as you step forward. In the missions, if you try to go too far (to flank the enemies) – more ones will spawn just in front of you. In my opinion, the planning aspect is very important for turn-based games.
Despite its flaws, the game really has potential.  I cannot recommend the single player experience right now, but the multiplayer is really engaging. The mission unpredictability (enemy spawning after you reach certain points) and too much random factor in shooting (and no way to affect this effectively) hit the game in a bad way though. Buy if you are really into tactical games (as the experience is really fun in the end), like multiplayer, or enjoy wh40k universe. Otherwise wait for early access to finish.

Monday Night Combat at a glance is a mix of Dota, Tower Defense, and Team Fortress 2 in one. The Dota aspects are in the idea of defending a Moneyball while spewing out minions to attack it. Tower Defense comes in as turrets to shoot these robot minions. The class based teams of Team Fortress 2 are in the characters players use to control their class. Now, the game adds its own series of unique spins by putting it in 3rd person and having its own challenges. The single player mode is to defend the Moneyball while multiplayer is to attack the enemy and defend the objective. Unique gameshow type minigames are in each mode, where players have the opportunity to shoot a mascot for prizes. Together as a mix it is confusing for newcomers to adapt to the style, but mastering it turns it into a load of fun. The technical aspects of the game mixed with its funny humor by characters and cartoony style make for a fun game. Monday Night Combat offers flexibility and humor in combination.

In Victoria II (1836-1936) you manage your country throughout the industrial revolution. The game engine feels dated because it lacks a lot of quality of life improvements and it doesn't look too pretty. Underneath the hood, there is a complex system that keeps track of the population in great complexity, and if there was a Nobel Prize for video games, then this game would've won it. But even if there is a lot of complexity underneath, you don't really have that many options with what you can do. The AI is not that great and is vulnerable to large military stacks. You can't have more than two great powers allied, and while this is a much too "gamey" mechanic for my taste, alongside "crises" that can appear, it can lead to a lot of volatile situations. In the end, the world can be a pretty dangerous and unforeseeable place. If you have a lot of states in your sphere of influence, then your game can transform in a very tedious mini-game to properly maintain and manage them, and of course you lack at least a proper notification system for it. Overall it's a good game, with good mods, which can keep you hooked for a long time, but it really makes you yearn for a Victoria III.

As a huge Devil May Cry fan, this game hold up the standards just as well as it's predecessors,
possibly even better (I'm looking at you DMC2).
From a general game perspective, it is a solid Hack and Slash game with memorable characters,
a simple but enjoyable story, and more importantly you get to beat the crap out of demons while being a total
badass. (Also it's pretty challenging so, if you don't like handholding- this is the game for you)
I've had and played this game for about 4 years now, and still love it dearly. (Although it only says 30 hours on Steam, I also played it a lot on PS3 later).
But recently I came to notice how low the Steam ratings for this game were, and I read through the reviews to see why.
From what I've seen, it's all in regards to the port itself, which is understandable.
I've personally never had a problem running the game on Steam (even without downloading patches or anything).
That said, I do think that the in-game references to the controls are complete jank, because they are based on a
numbering system for buttons that VERY unclear. This can be solved by a simple google search to see what each button
does. I don't think the frame-rate is optimal (especially for a hack and slash) but it's not unplayable,
I really didn't notice it all that much when I first got into the game, but only after I'd had my share of a variety
of hack and slash games and really came to know the genre, did I notice the difference.
I also never had a problem using a controller as the controller scheme menu is actually pretty easy to understand,
although customization is a bit annoying.
In summary:
I guess from my experience, I'd say the game is still worth is, especially during Steam Sales, assuming that you can run it.
Like I said, it is a bit jank here and there, and it's not an excellent port by any means, but if you are looking to have a
hack and slash game that's easy to run on most computers just to casually play whenever, this is the game for you.

Spacerangers is a simple concept of a 2D space game taken to the extreme . Don't let that minigame look fool you this game has a $60 worth of content . It has somewhat of a sandbox feel to it because you can progress through the game by fighting dominators,trading,doing quests or just being a pirate .
The main menu has a very nice custom gameplay options which you can use to make it harder or easier on yourself . Also you can get much better starting ship at the cost of some races hating you which is a risk vs reward option .
Probably the most important part of this game is just the fact that it is so visually uniqe and the soundtrack is amazing . It may not be a 3D space game but it still creates very immersive atmosphere .
There are several gameplay types that may appeal to different players . You have a turn based space combat, RTS style ground quests where game completly changes the way it plays , Text Missions for people who enjoy puzzles and twitch space combat inside black holes .
Last but not least is the element of random events. Sometimes you pilot can get a sickness and then you will keep getting money each month as donations from organization fighting that disease.
Each time you play the game you may run into a different problem . Sometimes some of the big bosses can come to your system location and kill everyone , forcing you to flee and adapt new tactics .If you set game on hardest diffeculty you can actually loose entire galaxy to pirates & dominators .
It really is a solid game in all aspects . My only complain is that I prefered Dominatos (robots) as main story villains and not Pirates in this expansion . The pirate faction has some issues though because you might get a quest to protect all ships in pirate system which is kidna dumb because its just nearly impossible to do without some serious luck .

This game is like a bunch of minigames all thrown together.  The main game is a spaceship/trading game,  you upgrade your ship and fight in turn based combat.  There's a lot of freedom you can be a pirate or trader for example,  different ships have different strenghts.  There's also a bunch of "text quest" minigames which are completely optional but can give you good amounts of credits to upgrade your ship,  some are really good but others are a bit tedious.   There's also optional RTS missions which I don't like much but they are short and give good rewards so I'll try each once and skip it if fail once.  The game is a bit of a mixed bag but the main game is solid and oddly addicting.  Early on you have to rely a lot on other rangers and military ships to fight the dominators (evil AI) but you can eventually become very powerful and hire up to 6 NPC ships and capture enemy systems by yourself.

I wanted to love this game. It looked so nice. But no, there are too many major flaws.
> FIRST HOUR
Let's start from the beginning with the tutorial. Got killed by a pirate who had more defense, better weapons and faster engine. GAME OVER!
Since i could complete the tutorial later, gues it was just a random encounter.
Still, in the beginning you cannot really fight. If you happen to be stronger then your enemy, he just escape to next planet, repair his ship or just wait. You won't get any exp, loot or bounty. Just a bill for ship repairs.
> MISSIONS
There are different missions available, each reward some cash and exp.
With a trader ship you can take on transport missions. But they are near impossible at the beginning, since your engine is way too slow for the set timelimit.
Later you get engines with 40 parasec hyperdrive. You just jump to your target and the missions get really easy.
There are even assassination missions.

Monday Night Combat (better abbreviated as MNC) has been compared to the likes of Team Fortress 2 and Defense of the Ancients (DotA). MNC pits you in a tug-of-war-like battle where teams, supported by AI controlled minions, attempt to push into their opponent's base to destroy the central structure, the "Moneyball". The combat system is akin to an RPG-FPS in that you level up as you kill enemy minions, players, or turrets. Leveling up grants you the ability to upgrade any one of three skills unique to each of the six classes.
All the while this is going on, an announcer will be making snide and crude comments which not only adds character to the game, but hilarity. This is a colorful, competitive shooter one should definitely not miss out on!

This is a really interesting game that tells a story about the clichés of gaming. It's like an RPG, but instead of upgrading your character, you upgrade the game itself. For instance, you might unlock "256 bit color" as opposed to 16 bit or "free roaming" as opposed to moving along a grid. Some areas even allow you to cycle from modern graphics and mechanics to older ones, allowing you to bypass some limitations introduced in more modern games. This makes for a very interesting and enjoyable way to solve puzzles.
You progressively move from a sidescroller to a game like Torchlight or Diablo, without lingering on one particular thing; except for random-encounters. Random-encounters appear literally every few seconds in specific portions (mainly fast-travel) of the game-- and it's terribly boring. The whole point of the game is to continure moving from one thing to another, except for some odd reason they decided to keep those through the entire game. Now, sometimes they're fun, but the main character only has one attack for the better part of the game. This really discourages exploration-- and it takes a lot of time, mainly because you are granted a mini-map very late in the game. (It's sometimes hard to find where you need to go with random-encounters interrupting you every few seconds.)
That aside, it's honestly a refreshing experience to see all the generations of gaming packed into one 3.5 hour game. The gameplay mimics the gameplay of the generation you are currently dwelling in, and it does it very well. It seems like a lot of time was put into Evoland, everything was polished well to fit with the various themes.
I think this game is worth it at full price for some people, but also would not be enjoyed by others. I certainly enjoyed it, and if anything I've said sounds interesting, I recommend that you give it a try.

For any fan of classic retro RPG games, ranging from Zelda: Link's Awakening through Seiken Densetsu and Final Fantasy up to Diablo, Evoland is worth checking out. The game starts out with a 4-bit Gameboy feel and slowly evolves as you play through unlocking different aspects of the genre. The sentence "You got XYZ" will become very familiar very quickly, and I say "very quickly" both because the game is short and evolves as a quick pace, which is one of my gripes. While the trip down nostalgia lane is very welcome, some of the game feel is progressed very rapidly (from one screen to another I had changed to 8-bit colour, then bumped almost immediately up to 16-bit).
The other issue with the game is that later on, once you have unlocked the turn based battle, XP, and a second character, the pace gets very tiresome. XP is awarded, but levelling up is pointless toward the end of the game since the final boss battle gives you a limited 12 HP hit counter anyway, GP awarded is useful to buy only a handful of items such as Potions which I never used because my secondary character has infinite MP and heal. At that point, random encounters become a time filler with no real reward, and just become a tedious chore to get out of the way.

is a short, moderately difficult precision platformer.
It's also really short one: I spent just 30 minutes beating it twice in a row.
Graphics are cute. The background music and sound effects remind of simpler 8-bit days and are generally fine. There's virtually no story or explanation for anything, so that checks out as well.
Controls are pretty slick... once you find them out. You see, the game doesn't instruct much. For instance, you'll realize that you can shoot fireballs (with E and left mouse button). However, the game doesn't instruct you that this key exists. There's some in-game instructions on finer controls, like that you can actually double-jump, and climb a rope by pressing 'jump', but it doesn't help much that it's through a confusing image.
Level design is quite good, with lot of variety, from spikes to appearing-disappearing blocks to jump pads. But like another reviewer said, there are some cheap portions, like a super-mushroom jump pad that blows you up to the ceiling towards spikes, that is virtually impossible to dodge on your first try. It's a good thing that respawning is fast and levels are short, so this is not too annoying: usually a few retries are needed anyway due to poor timing or jump precision.
After 11 levels and two adequately varied boss fights, I still think
is too short. Sure, it's only $1, but when a game takes 20 minutes to beat
I feel it's too short. A few levels and a boss fight or two more would surely alleviate, if not solve the problem.
Nevertheless,
is a decent platformer even in its transient content.

While most of the levels are fair, this game does a very poor job of introducing the player to new concepts. Every new obstacle is introduced immediately next to another hazard that you are guaranteed to bump into on your first run. I mean, the first enemy is firing at you while you're still trying to figure out what the controls are. No one told you that you have a double jump or a ranged attack until after you need to use them. The first bounce mushroom is located directly under spikes before we have any idea what it does. The first rope is over water and the rope does NOT work like you think it works. I know you're doing this on purpose, Strong Cube, but cheap deaths don't make a game hard. They make it frustrating and unpleasant. Super Meat Boy is hard, but it always gives you a moment to play with new hazards or tools. That way when you die, it's because you weren't good enough to win, not because the game didn't tell you all the rules.
The graphics are adorable. Ezy is cute enough that I don't want to violently murder them even after refusing to jump on objects other than spikes. The rest of the game looks nice, though many sprites don't seem to fit. Looks like the sprites were gathered piecemeal from various free sprite packs.
I love how the spiked boulders have collision physics even though they never slow down for longer than a second.
It's a decent game, especially for the price.

Welcome to Endless Legend. Take a seat and listen, as I unravel to you one of the best 4X games of the past few years.
First of all, there are some things to bear in mind when considering this game, and for some people, these might be off-putting at first, especially if approached in a mainstream or Civilization-like manner. The first thing to consider about Endless Legend is that it encourages experimentation and kindly invites you to leave dogmas and balance at the front door before you enter its universe.
So, onwards we go.
If you've played Amplitude's former 4X Sci-fi space game, you'll immediately feel familiar with some of the concepts here. Endless Legend is actually set in the same universe, but rather on a single planet, named Auriga. Gameplay itself and the UI is very similar to Civilization V and fans of this game will immediately feel at home. However, there are a few subtle differences.
Auriga's first impressions are breathtaking. The landscapes are beautiful to watch and behold, making the most of the fantasy theme which has been provided. Also, Auriga features 2 seasons. Games start at the beginning of Summer, and every once in a while, a short Winter will set in. However, this isn't just a cosmetic feature. Winters affect most aspects of gameplay, including military and economic aspects, and some quests can only be completed during a certain season. Winter itself is a pivotal mechanic to the storyline, as Winters will become longer and harsher as time goes by, and you must find a way to "fix" this or risk complete obliteration of Auriga.
Speaking of quests, they make a pretty big part of Endless Legend. While the main quest will eventually lead a civilization to victory, there are dozens of side-quests to be found across your journies, varying from mundane tasks (such as kill X creature, provide Y resources) to more compex ones, such as forming an alliance or capturing a town. Most quests actually have follow-ups and context, so they're not completely forgettable.
Auriga is also a very lively place. You will encounter roaming creatures and also native tribes. These tribes are akin to Civ5 city-states and can be persuaded through various means to join an empire and provide unique bonuses or units. And speaking of tenants, you share the world with the other civilizations. Amplitude made full use of the fantasy setting and created a set of wonderful civilizations, each different and with their own personality, charm and mechanics. While in Civ, all civilizations were technically the same, bar some variety in buildings and units, in Endless Legend, each civilization is completely different. For example, the Roving Clans are trade oriented nomads, able to move around their cities. They're so trade-oriented that they can't even declare wars, and must push through trade, diplomacy and alliances. The Necrophages, on the other hand, are on the opposite side of the spectrum, being an all-evil warmongering insectoid race which consumes everything and is constantly at war, not being able to ally with anyone. No matter who you choose to play with, the level of detail and artwork will surely surprise you.
Progress is done via eras and a tech tree. While not as excentric and confusing as the Endless Space tech web, the tech tree of Endless Legend is also not as bland as the one in Civ5, for example. What Endless Legend wants you to do is to encourage experimentation. Forget about linear tech progression or "must-have" technologies. You can go that path, of course, but you will not only be very slow in progression, but you will also feel that the tech tree is there just for the sake of being. Instead, it invites you to try a more daring approach.
You dont' *have* to unlock everything, from hero recruitment, to all the resource extractors, to all armor and weapon upgrades. Doing so is the obvious but also the blandest way. I found out that experimenting with lesser-mainstream approaches can lead to interesting results. For example, in a game, I skipped completely through a set of resource extractors in order to focus on more combat-oriented techs (like weapons+armor) without having to linger too much in early eras. I ended up reaching the fourth era first and having OP military which then resulted in a fairly easy late-game. Surprisingly, the other civs were pretty easy-going on trading the resources I was lacking, so I didn't really feel handicapped by skipping those extractors.
Also, I've also won with just one hero by skipping most militaristic tech and piling up economic and trading techs. I was the laughing stock of the game when i came to military, but funny enough, I didn't have to deal with any wars, as the other Civs were appeased by my edge in trading and economic "gifts", allowing me to spearhead through the main questline and win the game.
This, of course, would never be possible without a proper diplomacy system. Endless Legend's diplomacy system, fortunately, is one of the best I've seen. Trading of resources and tech is done by using a special resource called "Influence". Alliances and conflicts are also brokered the same way, which means that players who focus on Influence tech and buildings can easily become rulers of the world. The AI is also very well-done in this regard, with leaders having proper attitudes and reactions to diplomatic events.
Of course, when diplomacy fails, the swords do the talking. As all 4X games, Endless Legend features a combat system. As with the rest of things, its combat system is far from mainstream. Instead of using a simple die roll, each combat is resolved on a tactical battlefield, similar to ones in Heroes of Might and Magic games. However, there are very different mechanics.
While the battlefield itself is merely a "zoomed-in" version of the actual terrain, units are not exactly in direct control of the player. Each battle goes through seveal "phases", and the player can only issue pseudo-orders to units, in the way of "try to move here" or "try to attack that unit". However, during the resolve phase, units attempt to carry those orders but there is no guarantee that the action will succeed. This may happen due to the units being out of range or the path becoming blocked. While this can be frustrating for people who like total control of the battlefield, it is actually a more realistic approach to the battlefield, by making the player feel more of a general in command, rather than a God dictating each and every move of its underlings at any given point in time. The only problem arising is that sometimes, units' pathfinding might be awkward and inconsistent with the player's expectations. Fortunately, for such people, an automatic battle system is available, which is more than decent in resolving conflicts.
Overall, I would recommend this game to every 4X fan out there. However, I would like to stress again that this is not your average game which lets you comfortably settle into a comfort zone. Getting the best out of Endless Legend will mean having to avoid that comfort zone, experimenting a lot and thinking out of the box. Almost all aspects and challenges in the game can be resolved in more than one way and sometimes the optimal way to do it is not necessarily the most obvious one. This game rewards those people who dare go outside the comfort zone and that's what sets it apart from the rest. If you expect a game which emphasises balance, precise combat and a sandbox for you to expand your empire in, you will be disappointed.

This, ladies and gentlemen, is how you do a port.
After spending nigh on 15 hours with the PS3 version, there was no doubt left in my mind that Ground Zeroes was worthy of being a Metal Gear Solid game. Say what you will about the length of the main mission, but this game clearly makes a case for the term "content" being much more nuanced than how most people refer to it.
Camp Omega is the real star of the show in Ground Zeroes - feeling like an amalgamation of the very best levels from Thief, Hitman, and the Splinter Cell series in their heyday - and it reinforces how the stealth genre is more about the levels than anything else. Everything about Camp Omega feels like it was crafted by experts: The believable vantage points, the sparing-yet-dense use of both high and low grounds, the use of light and shadow, it's all there.
The PC version (both surprisingly and unsurprisingly) is the definitive way to play this game. The FOX Engine truly shines when left to flex its muscles on superior hardware. Seeing rainwater drip down the face of one of the many nameless soldiers I would chokehold into submission later on in the opening cutscene was the first sign of the capabilities of this new engine.
I feel like the bar has been raised impossibly high by Ground Zeroes as a prologue to the upcoming The Phantom Pain. If the levels in the full game can capture even a fraction of the craft seen on display in this game, it will be more than something special.

ONLY recommended FOR HARDCORE FANS !
Why ? Well, personally, i wasn't too much against the idea of payed prequel if it were something like good old "VR Missions" packs of tens or hundreds (which were free addons for updated editions of the games) on the new engine or the prequel mission would have decent length and a boss fight (like Tanker from MGS2). Sadly, there is none of that. Camp Omega area is super small, even "the admin building" is not a building but a box, and you don't "go inside" but around the walls.
There are serious gameplay issues:
• Turning auto-compensation / bad movement transitions: BB does additional movements that are not requested by user (This is especially embarrassing since MGS1 is known for its fluid controls and sharp turning). In a stealth game [especially of The Stealth Franchise] it makes a difference between successful manoeuvre or mission failure
• Wall sticking is replaced by clunky cover mechanic. Now BB tends to clumsily stick out of cover, wall throws/shots are almost impossible because line of sight is obscured while BB manages to stick out and be seen by enemies
• Bullet replenishment on save's reload. And that in the series that is known for putting player in interesting tactical situations, like having 3 bullets and empty mag for 7 enemies. Blasphemy !
• Aggressive health regeneration
• Enemies lie down indefinitely on the ground with their rifles beside them (that's just silly)
• Enemy telepathy & "reflex mode" instead of great MGS2 alert system
• Magazines are infinite
• You can't "cook" grenades or throw them slow and under or, better yet, control the arc (see Syphon Filter 1-3 for great example)
• Kaz never shuts the ♥♥♥♥ up on replay
• Konami hasn't bothered to put sword gameplay in Raiden's mission or update models for MGS1-styled mission
Some upsetting technical deficiencies:
• Camera is too shaky
• Geometry clipping
• Knocked out enemies and POWs sometimes disappear and suddenly reappear
• Mouse sensitivity for aiming is not adjustable and too big
• Additional mouse buttons are not recognized
• DOF is insanely overblown
• Critical settings like AA, DOF and exact level of filtering are not clearly exposed
• LOD changes are too visible
• PC version doesn't have "music import" even thought Steam has it's own music library now
Moreover, it has story inconsistencies too:
• Disastrous lack of cutscenes and dialogues
• How Snake can be "formerly known as Big Boss" if in the ending of PW (that GZ starts almost immediately after) he ordered to be called like that ?
• Paz's name is incorrect, it should be "Pacifica Ocean"

Stronghold Crusader is a somewhat obscure RTS designed around maintaining an efficient economy while also defeating an opponent in the traditional RTS sense. Peasants are the lifeblood of your castle as you struggle to feed them, keep them happy, and tax every last cent out of them in order to turn them into soldiers.
As the page says, it is a castle simulator, meaning you run a castle economy, can build castle walls in designs that are only limited by the imagination, and lay siege to your opponent's castles with trebuchets, rams, ballista, and catapults (and more).
The skirmish mode, map editor and Crusader Trail (50+ skirmish scenarios) highly enhance the replayability of this game. The AI comes in many flavors from the annoying and vindictive Caliph, to the overwhelming force of the combat loving Lionheart, or the "Zerg Rush" of the Abbot and his massed monks. Each AI adds a different level of challenge, and learning to take them all on is quite fun.
Despite being an older game, multiplayer can be accomplished with a tool such as Gameranger, and the multiplayer works quite well.
Overall I highly suggest any RTS lover to pick up Stronghold Crusader HD, it is quite a fun experience that no current game quite manages to capture.

The story if somewhat bland, entertains long enough to forget about it and focus on the gameplay which is outstanding by all counts. It combines fluid fighting of Batman "Arkham" style games with viceral gore of being a gladiator/centurion of Roman empire. Executions that performed on every enemy once certain amount of damage is done to them are numerous and varied, from single to double executions to environment executions, counting probably around 50 different kinds, although some will get repetetive after a while.
Additional challenge can be found in solo and 2 player arenas, however, once enough levels and equipment is gathered through random in-game currency purchases (earn gold in arena -> purchase a booster that contains guarantied 3 items of certain quality -< repeat), the arena becomes a bit too east. Without scalable challenge, interest will wane quickly.
However, survival mode (2 player only) pits you against unlimited enemies in 7 different arenas (most of them are ill suited for the purpose, but still very challenging) with a task to survive as long as possible while your health drains. At first, surviving past 10 minutes is a challenge, but with good equipment, 27+ minutes are possible and more skilled people will go far beyond that.
Game is extremely easy to learn but relatively hard to master. Visual rollercoster, great andrenaline rush.
If you ever wanted to be a Gladiator, this is it.

Monday Night Combat is a Multiplayer Third Person shooter with tower defense elements. Some people compare it to TF2 but other than some basic designs such as the class system I'd call that a lazy comparison. It plays and feels like an arena combat sports game where you are making a push towards the enemy money ball and with the help of your bots(creeps) you drop the shields and destroy it. The classes are a bit more hybridized that TF2. For instance there is a class that is like the medic and engy rolled together. You get to choose which stats to boost with money you earn through kills on bots and other players. You can also purchase and upgrade turret towers at fixed points in the map to slow the progress of the other team. It's a fun, cheap, sort of repatetive game that you can play when you want something a bit different. I'd recommend it but if you are looking for TF2 or some other shooter this one will feel different.

Before starting this review, I first want to say I like to play Casually and not play to win.
Counter-Strike Nexon: Zombies is a free to play Counter-Strike 1.6 mod that adds a few features to the game that had not existed on its old engine.
That being said, old engine = better fps on a old computer. Although I did see some times where my FPS would drop for no reason and sometimes the game would hang for a second or two, but that is very slight.
Dig into it enough, and it is basically a free version that allows you to play Counter-Strike 1.6 for free at no cost.
Surprisingly enough, you may notice the negative reviews and most of the time the topic is something about Pay to win. Although in some perspectives that may be true, that doesn't really affect the gameplay on most servers. Most of the time you will be put into bad players who are new to Counter-Strike and that is where the fun perspective comes in.
Although the idea of limiting weapons into a certain amount of days that it can be used is a very bad idea, it can easily be ignored since the rewards system is tremendous and you can basically grab crafting items for doing absolutely nothing.
Some negative things I noticed was the lack of a good ui. It is terribly hard to nagivate with no problem and overall seems more confusing, especially from a person who knows very well about navigating the menu. The settings are very, very limited. There is no quality options, the native resolution may come up after restarting the game a few times, sound options are misleading and confusing, the advanced options are not even advanced options but more like extra pointless options. It isn't too bad though, you still have the option to change the options into the original cs 1.6 (which made no difference to me).
Servers are usually dead and using a quick-entry to find a certain gamemodes just puts you into the most deserted servers possible.
Other than that, the shop IS COMPLETELY OPTIONAL and may not affect the gameplay (depending on the server you join).
I would recommend this game for casual players; but for game winners, I think something else might be for you.

With the recent port releases spanning from RYSE, Dead Rising 3, Assassins Creed Unity and Far Cry 4, i had a bad taste in my mouth of ports. The gameplay is as fluid as ever and graphics look incredible at 1080p running somewhere around 60fps with a FX-8320+GTX750Ti SC+12gb Ram. Even after completing the Main campaign the game shows me somewhere around 10% completion which means there is a plethora of other things left to do outside the campaign.

Veteran player since the original PS3/Xbox 360 release... sadly cannot enjoy this game anymore
I want this to be clear, I was once a MEGA Awesomenauts fan; at the time of the Kickstarter for the Starstorm expansion (back before I had a regular income) I was able to scrounge up enough to back the game into the Silver Koala tier, a choice that I now wonder if it was worth it or not. If my play time included how much I played Awesomenauts originally on console, I've definitely clocked in over a hundred hours into this game alone. But as of recent I cannot enjoy this game anymore for what may seem like petty reasons but they still effect me as a long time fan and supporter.
I'll get right into the biggest detractor for my gameplay experience thus far, the Starstorm expansion includes a character by the name of Sentry X-58. To put it bluntly Sentry is an over-powered, broken mess of a character that Ronimo, the developers, seems to refuse to acknowledge as such. Sentry X-58 is easy to learn, easy to play, and can carry your 3-man team to such a disgusting extent he made me stop playing the game upon his release because everyone was using him for an easy victory. Now, after nearly a year, I finally decided to give Awesomenauts one more chance being as how newer characters had been released since then. The first game was a complete wash as one player on the enemy team used Sentry-X58 and carried the team to a quick and brutal win, leaving my team to question why even bothering to continue when any 3 VS 3 team fights only lead to a slaughter. A Later game was going well early on until one enemy player ragequit and was replaced with a new player using Sentry X-58; in merely minutes we had almost lost and only won because of a successful backdoor play, it was a bitter victory that left a horrid taste in my mouth.
What frustrated me more so was the realization that Ronimo has seemed to refuse to understand or believe that Sentry-X58 is a broken character that will prevent players on the opposing side from having any fun. I recognize and understand that the developers at Ronimo are not going to listen to one negative Steam review but I can at least hope that I may sway some players to tell Ronimo to either nerf Sentry X-58, or re-work his entire character to something less broken and requires actual technique to play well. New players beware, the online community will not treat you nicely and Sentry X-58 players will more than likely make you ask for a refund on your purchase.

One word describes Evoland... Nostalgia.  Evoland respectfully pokes at the evolution of the action/adventure rpg genre.  You start with top down monochrome 8 bit graphics only being able to move right, and you have to unlock new evolutions to the game i.e. the ability to move left or up and down or music.  Every time I unlocked a new dimension to the game (in one case literally unlocking three dimensional graphics) I laughed and my inner child cheered as I memories of games I grew up with came flooding back.  They pull heavily from Legend of Zelda, Final Fantasy, Diablo, and even one liner nods to modern games like Skyrim.
My only real complaint with the game is the length.  You can easily beat it (including all of the "secrets" and extras) in a day.  But, that seems like a minor issue when you remember that the entire game was produced in just 48 hours.  I sincerely hope that they put out a more complete edition mostly because there are so many things still to satire.  I would love to see battle pets of a pokemon-esque nature and you never develop the abilty to jump or swim.  Still, all told I'm very happy with the what I got for only $10.

A brilliant old school game that manages to combine turn-based space exploration and combat, with text-adventure segments, a light-weight RTS minigame and a nice overarching story; all presented in beautiful hand-crafted graphics.

I loved this game during my childhood and now this is finally on steam and even remastered! What else could you ask for! This game is a mix of RPG/Sicescroller/2D-Space simulation and turn-based combat. Oh my, it's such a great game!
Be aware, the only available languages by default are english and russian, so if you are not very familiar with either of those, then you should refrain from buying it!
If you can get your hands on a localized retail of the original game, I do recommend it however, because the storytelling is great, the combat system in 2D space is fun and the galaxies require a lot of well tinkered strategy to be explored/liberated properly.

Multi-genre, Space RPG, land RTS, Text Quest, Arcade action in sub-Space and a universe of other things to do.
Be a pirate, a mercenary, ranger, trader or all of the above. Alien races, planets, Screw the universe or help it. Take it easy and relax or crank the difficulty and go hardcore into the battle.
Battle or evade enemies and find artifacts, make your own fleet or go solo. Buy, upgrade, and sell ships, weapons and modifications.
Lovely atmosphere and exploration, great music, classic sci-fi themed tunes and great humor across the board. The game got its own style.
Redone in full HD glory, with new tech support and insane ammounts of content over the course of 11+ years of updating, by loving developers and now, by a team of fans. Massive.
Impressive and a true testament of a love for the game by Developers and Fans.
Overall, a unique experience, highly recommended.

整體而言，夏日特價買這款羅馬之子果然是對的，打折後二十鎂，對一款8小時破關的遊戲算是值得的。RYSE 作為XB1的新獨佔作品，採取保守的市場策略。RYSE壓低單機的製作成本，而投入多人連線的市場。個人覺得單人遊戲內容，就主流59鎂標準是不夠格的，但如果是宣傳電影的同名遊戲則是滿分，不知怎樣是否看官們知道大概品質到哪呢?
角色評分(6/10): 這是充滿MAN POWER的電影，如果就瘋狂麥斯:憤怒道比喻，大概就是把五個妹都去掉的感覺。如果想看妹則建議換片，如果想看肌肉棒子的基情滿滿則大力推薦(腐女大概會喜歡)。
劇情(6/10): 雖然加入類似特洛伊等神明參戰的元素，劇情張力很夠，但感覺不太現實。主角為了羅馬拼死拼活平亂，王儲一下就拆台導致整個蠻族暴動。這實在是莫名其妙。基本上是個爽片，但不太需要在意劇情，大概就是這種感覺。
操作設計(8/10): 動作遊戲就像電影，劇情可以不需要，但動作不能太醜。手把的支援很好，即使動作苦手也可以用普通難度通關，而且打出漂亮的畫面。簡單易上手，但要很猛無傷也不是容易的事情，難度設計的拿捏掌握的不錯。
音樂(8/10): 如果喜歡古典風格的音樂，這片音樂作得不錯，音樂好聽到打整天感覺都不會累，單獨拿出來放整天聽也很適合。

The beauty about this game is that it takes the Star Wars universe and creates its own story, its own characters, and its own lore.
The gameplay is your basic D20 RPG game, but it does a damn, fine job at it. There are many different dialogue options to choose from—many which influence the story and gameplay. Character customization is pretty versatile as well, although aesthetics aren't much so. Combat is turn-based, but its in real time with the ability to pause and select your next moves/powers.
The plot is amazing. George Lucas can definitely learn from the writers of this game, because the story is extremely interesting and engaging. The originality of it is also refreshing, as you get to explore the Star Wars universe from a different time period, with all new friends and foes.
Overall: Definitely an awesome game for any Star Wars or RPG fan out there.

A magnificent game, accompanied by inspiring music and the feeling of dominating an entire continent as your backwater country develops into a greater form of itself. Singleplayer is marvellous and ignoring some problems with the budget not showing the correct calculations, it works without a flaw! It mainly consists of you, the ruler of this country, attempting to 1. survive as a country; 2. strive to achieve everything necessary for the prosperity of your country; 3. resist the liberal and socialist threats to your absolute monarchy (unless you make the very poor choice of a democracy as your country). This "campaign" is very interesting in itself and completely sufficient for hours of entertainment and excitement. The multiplayer does however present a problem. Only LAN multiplayer is simple, trying to play with other friends requires one of those rather dubious multiplayer port-forwarding programmes, ones I do not have positive experience with (although others will argue that they are perfect). The games themselves work very smoothly, if playing with friends it is also more pleasurable to negotiate when to pause the game. A major setback however, is the cost of the game, but I believe it is worth the expense (with the "Heart of Darkness" DLC). The game, if one looks beyond its initial complexity and unexiting appearance, is thoroughly enjoyable, very engaging and a good source of some general knowledge. It is also very entertaining how small, regional conflicts can grow. An example I can give from personal experience is the "War of the Bavarian Conquest of East Switzerland". I, as Bavaria, desired to grow my territories and thus declared war on Switzerland. My Austrian ally joined me in my war. My army was intially destroyed by Switzerland (by some miracle) and Austria heavily intervened, destroying the entire Swiss army. France did not fail to notice this situation, and declared war on my alliance. Switzerland promptly surrendered and East Switzerland was now Bavarian. The Bavarian empire had begun. I had no further interest in the war and negotiated peace with France. My war was now being led by Austria against France, the combat of whom led to a mutural destruction of their respective armies.
Utterly, utterly magnifivent game, it deserves recognition and the cost!

-The grenades. Both when I use them or the enemy throws them at me. You trow a grenade at a group of enemies, you're lucky if you kill 2 of them. -The difficulty ramp between world 3 and 4. To be homest, it's not that big of a deal, after some playthroughs. And I get it, you're in the late-game and the boss is aproaching. But you enter level 4-1 and all of the sudden, everybody is wielding heavy machine guns and snipers. And don't even get me started on those ducks withs glasses. Fudge them.
-Achievements that require a lot of grinding. I'm looking at you "Endless Veteran", "Gun Nut" and "Modern Hunter". It just breaks my little completionist hearth.
-Cheaply difficlut Endless Mode. You spawn with the default loadout of your choosen character; ammo, weapons, medkits, grenades, and overshields are rare to come by; every floor or so, you get a debuff or the enemies get buffed and the focus on getting Bounty is just too big. Why? Well, between worlds you get a special shop where you can buy consumables, relics and better weapons, upgrade the weapon you're already holding or get rid of those pesky debuffs/buffs. "That dosen't sound too bad" you may say to yourself. The problem is, most of the time, you won't have enaugh bounty the complete more that 2 of these purchases. What ends up happening is: you move level to level, ammo and health gets low, your weapon no longer holds up to the enemies, said enemies get more stronger because of the buffs, while you get weaker because of the debuffs. In 13 hours of playing I never completed the first loop. And the game expects me to get 50 loops if I want to 100% the game? Sorry, I'll skip.
-Minor bugs to the menu and occasional white screen at boot-up.
Closing remarks:
I know that the list of Cons seems bigger that the one of Pros, but I can't deny the fact that I had a blast playing with all the characters, unlocking the relics and getting the achievements, even if not all of them. So yeah, I recommend this game if only for the Adventure Mode. And most of all, It's free, so why won't you give it a try?

My first impression of this game was extremely positive. The first thing that hits you is the exceptional, laid-back, atmospheric, synth driven music that reminds me of Tangerine Dream and provides a psychologically potent contrast to the busy work environment.
Some of the levels are also are a true joy to drive around, in particular the various buildings in the production facility, although the technical standard of the graphics is nothing to get excited about and there's a nasty amount of pop-in.  The tasks are varied enough to keep you interested. They are chosen randomly so that each time you play the level, you will be moving boxes from different places. This is a questionable idea for the time attack mode, as it introduces an element of luck instead of it being pure skill, but this randomness does work for the the main game where you are given a time limit and you get given more time when you complete the task. For both modes, it can keep you engrossed in a level for a lot longer than you would expect and keeps them replayable.
The free play mode is not great. You can move some boxes around, create a few walls, fail in your attempts to create stonehenge and create some crude pixel art, but ultimately it isn't minecraft, the pieces aren't designed for this purpose. It doesn't allow for great amounts of creativity and so you will find yourself spending the majority of time in the modes that give you structure and a reason to be there.
Sadly, as much as I wanted to like this game, and as much as I would have liked it if the implementation was done correctly, there were some problems that mean I can't really recommend it.
The biggest problem that I had with the game was the poor implementation of box physics... This is something that is fairly essential to get right in a game about moving boxes with a forklift truck. When raising or lowering a box, gravity seems to effect it only in steps, so you can lower the forklift just a small amount and it will not move the box, it will be hovering in the air (it could be a problem to do with raising and lowering when tilted). You will see these problems in the jerking movements of the boxes and it can sometimes lead to unfair failures, particularly in the last port level where it is extremely noticeable and exaggerated due to the size of the containers. You can pick up a crate in this level, tilt backwards, notice that the crate remains totally unmoved, move the forklift down a bit so it is hovering in the air and then you can even drive off with it remaining magically unmoved in the air until you are totally clear, at which point it will drop to the floor.  Boxes also don't seem to have much weight, your forklift will happily pick up huge crates and even stacks of crates upon crates without causing balance issues.
As good as the music is, there are only three tracks.
You can drive straight through people... Not a huge deal as it's not a game about killing, but other games like Driver handle this by having pedestrians at least attempt to avoid the vehicle instead of walking straight through it.
Altogether, it showed some promise, but given the poor implementation, it is difficult to recommend at full price. The only reason to buy it is because of the soundtrack and the fact that there aren't many other games to choose from that are about forklift trucks.

As a long time MGS fan I was ecstatic to see METAL GEAR SOLID V: GROUND ZEROES appear on Steam. The storyline is best appreciated if you have played the previous games in the series but, unlike MGS4, there is very little that will leave newbies confused. Ground Zeroes marks a distinct maturation for Kojima's writing - this time the big concept (torture) is not marred by goofy tonal changes. Granted, there is a character called Skullface, but that's about as far-fetched as it gets.
OK, GAMEPLAY:
Initially I was concerned that the new additions to the series - such as being able to mark enemies, go into bullet-time slow-mo upon being detected and, crucially, Kiefer Sutherland as the new voice of Big Boss (!) - were concessions to casualising the series. Upon playing Ground Zeroes, I realise this couldn't be further from the truth. Kojima has provided one of the most brilliant, dynamically evolving AI toyboxes I've encountered since Grand Theft Auto 4. All the new techniques are a welcome addition to a series that was beginning to feel a bit long in the tooth and, most importantly, do not skewer the difficulty curve. Animation is fantastic, with Big Boss being an utter joy to control on either controller or keyboard. I actually prefered keyboard controls for aiming accuracy, although the lack of analogue control is a drawback to this method.
Much has been made of the fact that Ground Zeroes is a glorified demo. I would argue that the sandbox gives you the scope and tools to play literally for however long you desire. You can theoretically complete the game in 20 minutes but, aside from speedrunning, where is the fun in that? MGS fans know they will get their moneysworth, and Ground Zeroes serves as the perfect introduction to a true gaming institution for those not 'in the know'.
Special props to the PC port: Namco, this is how you do it! As of now this is the 'best' version of Ground Zeroes, running smoothly and looking gorgeous on the most humble of toasters. I've encountered no crashes, glitches, or slowdown since playing.

Space Rangers HD is a very niche open-world turn-based space trading and combat strategy game that I think many people will find rather frustrating.  The game is improperly balanced so that the player has a very narrow path to success and a steep learning curve.  There's a lot of different ships and parts you can use, but many of them seem not to be viable and will lead to your death.   Not enough firepower?  You die.  Not fast enough?  You die.  Not earning enough income to pay off pirates or repair your ship after fighting them?  You die.   Not enough fuel make a hyperspace jump to run away?  You die.  The learning curve and narrow path to success reminds me very much of the game X3: Terran Conflict, another more-complex open-world space trading and combat game which I would recommend over this.  If you are able to find the path to success then you may enjoy these games greatly, but if you fail to find it you will die again and again without making much progress and probably give up the games without experiencing what they have to offer.
In this game you are supposed to try to control the pirate threat but you aren't powerful enough to kill pirates early in the game, only fast enough to chase them around and sustain a lot of damage fighting them only to have them land on a planet and fully repair their ship most of the time.  Before you know it the whole universe starts getting overrun by pirates and you have only been able to kill one or two strays.  You start to get jumped by more pirates than you can afford to pay off or hope to kill off, run out of money, then die.  Prepare to save and reload often in this game as that seems to be the main path to survival when you don't know what you may encounter before entering a black hole or a sector or taking a quest.  Death is going to find you, so be sure you have saved before that.
Some of the planet battles in the game are difficult and frustrating and will require many restarts in some cases before you randomly end up with the right plan and conditions that will allow you to succeed.  You can skip them if you want to as the game does have an option to do that.
There is some gaming population that will find games with narrow success conditions and an abundance of options, many of which are superfluous or serve to hide the narrow path to success fun to play.  These players enjoy overcoming difficulty and pride themselves in their ability to analyze a situation and find a way to succeed.  They will find the way to exploit weaknesses, recognize patterns, and filter out what doesn't lead to success.  They require a certain amount of failure to make victory worth achieving.  If all or even most players succeeded, then the challenge would not be great enough for them.  If this sounds like you, then you may enjoy this game.  If that doesn't sound fun to you, then you probably should pass on this one.

Warehouse and Logistics Simulator is a simulation game developed by the team at app2fun. This is a single-player only game and is currently at the time of writing this review available for £3.73 in the UK but its full price is usually £10.99.  This game was released on the 25th February 2014 on steam and has received many mixed reviews. Some people have said that " its the kind of games old ppl love 10/10" and others have said "WTF nothing like a real fortlift 0/10". I will give my options on the game.
Firstly when you are taken to the in-game menu you are greeted with a quite poorly designed menu with some very bad music that is on loop. The Menu has only a few buttons these are: Standard Game, Time attack, Free Play, Options, Credits and Quit game. I shall now go down the menu in this order reviewing each part.
Standard mode is the main part of the game in which you can unlock the different areas. When you click on the standard mode you are presented with the different areas with different forklifts, There are a total of 5 different areas in the game these include a department store, high bay warehouse, production facility, construction site and a port. These are all locked at the beginning of the game apart from the department store. When you load the game you see at the top of the screen a score counter and a time counter. In this mode you are instructed to go and collect and take pallets of objects to the designated area in a certain amount of time. If you do around what i believe is 3 pallets you get a new task which is the same and eventually you unlock the next area.
This is the same concept as before but instead of working to unlock different areas all you are instructed to do is transport as many good and pallets as possible in the specified time.
This is as simple as it gets all this mode is, is as stated no rules or time limit, and to go around as you please.
The options menu is very very simple and very lacking any customisable options. The game options allow you to choose from 6 different languages English, German,French,Spanish,Italian and Polish. The option menu also allows for not very many graphical options. You can choose from high, medium and low graphics quality, anti aliasing on or off, SSAO on or off and HDR on or off. You can also choose the resolution up to 1080p but sadly there is no windowed mode button.  Finally there are different options for the audio such as Overall volume, Music Volume. Oh and there is also mouse sensitivity and invert y-axis. This options menu is very disappointing especially since it doesn’t contain and control configuration but the game has very basic controls. W,A,S,D for moving the forklift. Up,Down,Left,Right for operating the forks and then 1,2,3 for the different camera angles.
Standard credits.
That’s up to you.
Overall i would say this game is only for those who are desperate to play a forklift simulator as this has no unique selling points and even at that i would say only buy this is it is on sale as this game is a very lacking game. Only featuring 5 areas, bad spelling within the descriptions such as in free play mode “transport as many good as you life". This game feels as if it was rushed or just ported over to steam to try and make a bit more money. I wouldn’t recommend this as there are other fantastic simulators such as Euro Truck Simulator 2. I would only recommend this is you are a diehard simulator fan or are very bored and looking for a laugh or two.
Rating: 4/10

Putting my system specs here first because there are a lot of complaints on bad optimisation.
GTX 960 4GB
Stock CPU (Intel @2.9GHz)
Stock 8GB RAM
The only additions I made to my PC was the GPU and PSU.
I play this game on 1080p on a mix between medium/high settings and get 50-70fps so unless you have a school-computer or apple product I'm sure you can run this game fine with some tweaks to resolution/overall settings because I did before I upgraded from my stock GPU...
As for the actual game, its really well done:
+ The UI is amazing
+ Creates a great battle royale scenario
+ You can create your own lobbies with your own rules and multipliers
+ Get into games very quick, maybe a max of 2 minute wait times pre-lobby
+ There are so many different ways to play the game (e.g. Guns, Melee, Ninja, Dinos, etc.)
+ Incorporated party system to allow you to play with/against friends
+ Player customisation
Although some problems I've found
- Some extinction events drop mobs directly on your head, maybe a Spino spawning on top of you might possibly damage your chance of survival! Maybe if they were dropped within a small radius of you so you had a chance to avoid it. (Same with the bug swarms)
- The player customisation is cool, but you can create some advantages for yourself, by changing skin tone and size you minimise your hitbox and you can hide in the shadows better than those using other skin tones which allow for some sneaky plays or just being too small for them to hit you
- No way to spectate a game when you die and you have no one left in the party to spectate/ are in a free-for-all
From the time I've played currently, I'd give it an 9/10, the mob-dropping extinction events being what stop it being the perfect experience for me, but its still a great game that I will enjoy playing for a long while!

This is a short and sweet run through the history of RPGs and adventure games. There will be many familiar elements to those of you who've played the Final Fantasy and Zelda series, especially FF6, FF7, and LttP. (And if you haven't, then what the ♥♥♥♥ are you waiting for, an engraved invitation? Seriously, they're amazing games.) There's even a section that plays like Diablo. The game starts out simply, with graphics that would be at home on the original Game Boy, and expands down the timeline of advances in game design and technology. Those of you who, like me, grew up with that progression, will appreciate this trip down memory lane.

Let me start this review by saying I didn't play this game anywhere near launch (started only recently), and have had very little experience with the Devil May Cry series before I started playing this game. I did have experience playing God of War, Ninja Gaiden Sigma and the like before however, so I'm familiar with the Hack & Slash genre.
With that said, here is my review. You're free to disagree with my points (I'd be more glad if you did agree though :)) as this is my personal opinion.
First of all, the story. I kinda liked it, although it wasn't unusually gripping or emotional.  I don't want to spoil anything to people who haven't played it yet, but I will say that thanks to Dante's entertaining persona, the memorable bosses, and a few nice plot twists I didn't expect, it's one of the better plots for this type of game I came across. 7/10
The gameplay. This game has the best combat I've ever seen in this type of game, with great flow, especially on Turbo mode. Trying out different load-outs (there are plenty of combinations of arms, and most weapons are unique and fun to use) and styles (essentially a selectable special move to go along with your weapons) is addicting, and enemies (bosses in particular) are varied and require different strategies rather than repetitive mashing or QTEs to beat (looking at you, God of War).
Exploration and puzzles were a bit too simplistic for me most of the time, but helped make this game feel more like a grand adventure than a static arena.
The controls in the game however are problematic. While I've got them to work perfectly with my Logitech F310 (in D-Input mode) and Net Way PS3/PC Gamepad, This game doesn't support Xbox 360 and One controllers without some tweaking, so I recommend having an older, Direct-Input controller to play with as Keyboards aren't optimal for this type of game. 10/10 (with a gamepad, otherwise 6. yeah, it's that important)
The graphics of the game are showing their age; it is a relatively old game, and doesn't support high resolutions. Also, the graphics of this version are inferior to the PS2 and HD Collection versions as some of the more advanced lighting and shadowing effects are missing, and there is some very mild lag in some areas. The game is still perfectly fun and playable with these faults, but it's still something to keep in mind though if you care a lot about visuals. The character and environment designs however were pretty good for their time, and still have a bit of charm, even today. (7/10)
The music here is a mixed bag: I'm not a fan of the heavy-metal esque battle themes, although they fit the setting of the game. The rest of the music, like ambient sounds and effects are immersive however, and the goddess statue and final boss themes were very nice IMO. (6.5/10, although if you like the battle themes you might give an 8 or a 9)
Finally replayability. This game isn't very long (about 12 hours for my first playthrough) but has immense replay value, with a lot of harder difficulty levels to unlock and test your skills with, an alternate playable character with unique weapons (Vergil), the ability to carry your upgrades and items from playthrough to playthrough, and the Bloody Palace, an arena with near endless battles, this game can keep you busy for a very long time if you want to master it. 10/10.
Verdict: DMC3 SE is a fantastic game, with a ton of replay value. If you have a gamepad and don't mind a minor graphical downgrade, this is a solid reccomendation. If you're with a keyboard though or want the best graphics available, I'd recommend getting the PS2 version/HD remake if you can. Even if you can't, there's still a very solid game here. (No final score, as there are too many variables depending on your hardware and everyone has their own priorities in games. I only try to advise. Who am I to judge what you find important?)

I don't have a huge amount of time to play games, but the Amplitude Games have something special about them. Between the core game and the recent add-ons this has a lot of replayability. And it was already a game I'd played through several times, just to use each race and explore their uses.
Each race is genuinely unique, with an art style that is a breath of fresh air. You'll find your favourite soon enough. Some require very different approaches or you'll fall behind opposition races quickly.
While tropes of the genre including resource gathering, building an army, creating new cities and conquering existing ones are here as usual Amplitude have blended them in a way that gets more out of them and pushes each element a little further than I've seen before. You can see influences from the Civilisation series. It's not so much you haven't seen some of this before, it's that you haven't seen this done quite this way.
For example while you follow a shared tech path, there are some techs specific to each race, and on more difficult settings, you can't afford to research every tech advance at every level. Access to new levels is unlocked after you hit a threshold of research, so you can advance ahead of other races quickly enough if you're playing one of the more tech focused races and have set up enough defences to hold off invaders. But it's a balance between competing demands. You need to think which technologies will support and compliment your strategy overall. Some techs are essential but others can be skipped over if you're on a war footing. Some races can buy most of what they need, others need to focus on cities producing what they need. You might choose to work towards a later version of armour, ignore the intermediate armour advances for example. But each armour/weapon type unlocked requires mines for resources at that level. This sounds complex, but the way the game unfolds and reveals the resources ( when discovered ) works very well. Something complex made easy.
There are few base troop types per race, you either upgrade these ( extensively under categories of armour and shields, weapons and accessory items ) These have the usual bonuses, individual or group based with some providing considerable complimentary boons. Each race has a cavalry, archer and warrior base type. With the Guardians expansion you have access to demi-god like giants. While the number of troops isn't huge, the customisation you can apply effecitvely multiples your troop type options. You can through equipment build fast moving units out of base types, hard hitting units, more defensive units, stealth units ( with the latest expansion ) and so on.
Hero experience gain is also good, with advances for a hero usually providing options to either boost a city you've assigned them to or boost the army they are marching with. As with troops you equip heroes with weapons, accessories and armour.
If there's one minor negative for me it's the tactical combat itself. It feels a little less engaging than I'd like. I think they wanted to streamline the time it takes to resolve battles and have made an effort to reduce a lot of the setup time for these you'd normally have in the genre. It's personal taste, but I'd like more room to maneouvre and direct control of units. ( You choose stance, aggression or defence, you choose targets, then rounds play out like a pre-set card game and you choose again after a few rounds ) It's passive. On the other hand the stats are clear, and the equipment of troops plays a huge difference so equipping troops with the right equipment can make a huge difference.

Wow, this game was amazing when it was just a mod to the full game but man did they put in some serious work polishing it up. It a very hard game that is very easy to be casual in. So far I have waited at most 5 minutes to get into a game and this was at 4 am cst. Every match was full.
The pro:
-Intense hunger games style game mode (don't slack off or you will die right away).
-Way more variants to choose from over the original mod (FFA, 2pl team, 4pl team, 6PL TEAM!)
-gameplay is smooth as butter and your shots (for the most part) hit where they should.
-Start with all engrams unlocked which, imo, is a huge QOL inprovement.
-Winning earns you permanent hats!
-Insane replayability (many different creatures to tame and build your strategy around and the loot drops are always wildly different causing you to change your tactics on the fly).
-Graphics are still as gorgeous as they were on the full game (Im running on medium with no FPS issue whatso every).
-HOLY CRAP THEY FIXED THE LOAD TIMES! For you that didnt play before, it used to take the mod at least 3-5 minutes to load. Now they have a beautiful lobby system in place and the loading on the same hardware is nearly instantanous. HUGE plus in my book.
-FREE!
Cons:
-Undeniably, there is still some compatibility issues. It seems like the better your hardware, the worst the game will run. When I booted up the game I did have to spend about 5 minutes in the settings to tweak it to run smooth (expected from any game let alone one that is Early Access). My reccommendation is to turn sky quality and ground clutter all the way down and then if you still lag, you should start lowering the resolution scale. If it still lagging for you there, then there are more advanced tweaks to use that will adjust the launch commands. Still lagging after that? Your PC is too bad or too good and not optimised for the game (give it a few weeks and come back they are always updating!) For reference, I am running 8gig ram, a GTX750, and an intel i5.
-Many racists and immature children that you have to confront in the lobby and game. While I take a sick pleasure in killing these guys first or stalking them to toy with them, some may be put off by this. Remember this is a mod and there is no moderation unless you go on the unofficial servers.
-Ingame chat (both voice and text) is lacking. Not the biggest of issues because Discord is almost always better anyways.
Overall, I am very shocked and pleased with how this mod came out in the standalone version. I would have payed again for it, tbh. It is that good and only going to get better. The fact that they just decided to release it for free and do a huge tourney is just amazing. I really hope they continue to optimize the game so that more can play and that they continue to add QOL features. As far as the content already in is concerned, its nearly flawless (compared to how it was 6 months ago).

The gameplay is frantic, strategical, and always a blast to play. But it's really the stylized characters and writing that help to make the experience so memorable. This game has went through significant improvements from it's first release and the pay-to-win aspect is not as apparent as other players make it seem. This game holds a lot of fun game modes and the community is relatively nice as both new and experienced players can easily get into a PvP match with little introduction.
When my friends and I first downloaded this game, we jokingly wanted to play a game with poor reviews just to see how bad it was, but surprisingly we ended up playing two five-hour sessions considering how fun it was. Honestly, we were expecting an inbalanced game of pay-to-win players and the usual hack sessions that comes with the CS 1.6 experience. Surprisingly however, the game did not seem to have much, if any, people hacking to win.
At first glance, the game seems unfair as zombies can either be blown to oblivion by the surviving humans or humans can be overwhelmed by a zombie spawning amongst a "cheap" spot. To be fair, this game encourages your knowledge of well defended positions and map usage to either survive or flank your enemies.
What really makes this game come to life is the usage of the glitches present and the stupidity that comes from being chased down by a horde of zombies or hanging off a ledge while zombies use their abilities and grenades to pick you off. Essentially the game becomes a glorified hide-and-seek or king of the hill as you try to survive against other players in your favorite CS maps.
Another enjoyable aspect of the game is the mission modes such as Escape and Shelter that puts a different spin on the game with new maps that are custom made to this game. Escape was a fun run and gun mode that has you scrambling to reach the exit in different areas; while Shelter was a survival mode where you protected your base from hordes of NPC zombies as you scrounge for both supplies and money as you build up turret defenses and walls to secure your dwelling.
One of the downsides of the game is the lack of tutorial for some of the new game modes as they only teach you the PvP and survival modes in the beginning. So in some of the PvE modes you're going to either rinse and repeat a lot to understand what you need to do or hopefully have a more experience player show you the ropes, which actually does occur fairly often.
A downside of the game, which in my opinion does not affect gameplay too much, is the need to continutally create weapons and items via blueprints to keep utilizing the higher end ones. However, as powerful as the guns are, they seem to little much in PvP modes as most of the time you would need a whole squad to help kill a zombie.
Another aspect that seems unnecessarily difficult to process is the user interface as it mostly seems crowded and sometimes difficult to find certain objects you want to use such as costumes and guns that are on a limited time usage. Although after a few minutes of use, it becomes relatively understandable to use albeit dated.
This game feels like a throwback to old school games where you would do the cheapest thing to live. And that's good. Part of the enjoyment comes from unintentionally phasing through floors or on top of objects to find a once-in-a-while hiding spot and compared to most zombie survival games where you must rely on more of the traditional map knowledge and weapons to win.
This game received a lot of poor reviews from when it was first released and even though it seems like a dated game with new modes, it's a lot of fun to play when you just want to BS around and have some stupid fun to your line up.
