Another excellent chapter in the Higurashi series. Watanagashi delves deeper into the shocking secrets of Hinamizawa. What starts as a another slice-of-life drama soon turns into a chilling-to-the-bone thriller. One of the finest VNs on the Steam and well recommended to all who who enjoy an excellent story. Writing is again superb. You will be masterfully manipulated until the very end. Let's hope the next chapter comes soon.

Remember that Watanagashi isn't so much a computer game as it is a visual novel. In this VN, you're basically reading a novel with pictures, backdrops, music and sound effects thrown in for good measure. I think it makes good use of those elements to help sell the story by setting the mood for the reader, but your results may vary.
I enjoyed the anime series a while ago, and I continue to enjoy these VNs as they come out. They flesh out the anime's story which came out at a breakneck speed. On this 'replay', I also have to credit the writers on how far ahead they thought about certain story elements while using misdirection. I don't want to spoil the storybecause that's part of the fun of murder mystery stories.
Last time, I wrote down a list of Things I Learned in Hinamizawa. My list was considerably longer, but I narrowed it down to the ten I thought would best fit the events of the game and my impressions.
- Learn to see things from other people's point of view, or risk exploitation when they use this ability against you.
- Keep fighting until the last minute. "As soon as you give up, it's all over."
- It is just as important to talk about your feelings as it is hard to do so.
- When you are trying to patch things up with someone, don't assume everything is alright just because you are on speaking terms again.
- Ghost stories will never go out of fashion, for better or worse.
- Do not underestimate mankind's capacity for cruelty to what he deems less than himself.
- Lying is much harder than telling the truth. You can't keep the fake facts straight forever
- Someone else might have to pay the price for your mistake, even when you really want to take responsibility for it.
- You might not like what you find, but you must always persue the truth
- Sometimes a person really is too far gone to help. Your best effort won't go unnoticed by them, but you'll only hurt yourself and others.
Not as good as part one, but it's essential and highly enjoyable. Cannot wait for the rest of the series to be up on Steam!

Excellent chapter on Mion
As you can tell from the title art, this chapter focusses on Mion and her sister (I don't think this qualifies as a spoiler since you can easily infer this piece of information from the descriptions of several achievements...). The story feels larger this time. Also we get to know more aspects about the characters and the village Hinamizawa. As a fan of the anime adaptation, I enjoyed this chapter a lot, discovering all the minute but interesting details that were omitted in the anime.
In summary:
Pros:
+The twins theme of Mion/Shion is brilliantly explored. Depending on the context, the writing is funny, entertatining, or horrifying. Also, the twins theme echos well with the duality theme of village Hinamizawa (the bright and dark sides of the village).
+The pacing has been improved. The last chapter has a very slow and sometimes boring start, featuring numerous club activities that have little contribution to the main plot. Not this time. The main story starts rather early on. Also, the story progresses smoothly, compared to the last chapter.
+New background music an better BGM switching.
+Sound effects are utilized better.
+Rena still rocks!
Cons:
-The reader will be introduced to the curse of Oyashiro-sama in a boring exposition... for the second time ... as if we hadn't got enough in the last chapter.
-The thoughts of the protagonist are written in a really repetitive fashion.
-Although this is chapter dedicated to the character Mion, I cannot find any new portraits for Mion (aside from Shion of course), which is really disappointed.
Overall, I strongly recommend buying it at full price. Looking forward to the next chapter!

Monday Night Combat is a 3rd-person shooter, whose objective is to destory the other team's moneyball with small arms fire. The catch is, however, that you can't destroy its initial shields yourself - AI controlled bots for your team must do that. Thus, you must escort them, destroy enemy bots, and let them bring down the shield so that your human players can finish the job.
In practice, this game focuses less on racking up kills and soloing objectives (a near-impossible task), and requires teamwork and killing AI bots more than other players, which results in rewarding kills and less frustration for players who often have trouble staying alive.
All the classes have their niche, and it is actually quite difficult to be a liability to your team. Even if you can't kill other players or stay alive for long, you can contribute greatly by stopping the advance of enemy teams' bots. This alone, in my opinion, makes the game a lot less frustrating than team-based shooters usually are.

I've been wanting to play this game for a while now, but I don't have a PS4/Vita to play it on so I wasn't even waiting for this to get to PC, but would you look at how things work out and it did indeed get ported.
Anyway, just finished with the last Achievement (The Land Without Night) and I would say the game is worth it to me. Here's a little more detailed.
Pros
- Probably one of my favorite soundtracks in a game. There wasn't a track I didn't like and there is generally quite a few I don't like in games (Ori and the Blind Forest is one of the very few exceptions as well)
- While the setting is not very original, they made their own take on it with a female protagonist and another female support character and made it (more or less) their love story. The plot is pretty much an anime though it's in game form
- The character designs fit with the characters and the Servans also make sense gameplay-wise (it would've been very odd if they didn't)
- Dynasty Warriors-like combat mechanics. In the sense that it's of the X, X, X and X, X, Y style combos. There is a slight downside but I'll get to it in the cons, though not as big of a downside as it could've been.
- Quite a few hidden extra scenes between Arnice and the cast amidst various chapters if you just go and explore through previous explored zones. (Like Lilysse get laundry detergent for Arnice's clothes, encountering the Professor 'researching' various fiends or coming across Lloyd and see what money-making scheme he's thought of)
- Absolutely no problem with framerate and after they patched the CPU usage problem it's running like a charm.
Cons
- No Exit Game button. Didn't think I'd ever say that about a game.
- The combat as I said is a plus, but in this game it's a little dumbed down and you can't get aerial combos or if there are, I'm not doing it right. In DW when you level up, you get additional combos for your weapons, in this game there's no new combos. When you get the weapon, that's all the combos you'll get. Now that's slightly subverted by having a skill that lets you freely change between weapons when you're attacking, so It's not as big a deal as I'm probably making it out to be.
- Limited animations for expressing themselves and also immobile hair that's very visible in various scenes. There's also no walk animation for Arnice when outside of the hotel or the altar which could've been easily added or taken from said places and just altered it for the different weapons.
- The shadow quality in cutscenes and when there's dialogue between the characters is noticeably bad. I don't know why that is, since there's no problem with it during gameplay.
- Wouldn't really say it's a con, but it's a shame there's no real NG+. Going through the story again with all upgrades and having enemies that are 3-4 levels above you even if you can't level again, it would just need to drop slightly better items.
I may have missed a few things, but overall I really loved the game, and if I had a PS4/Vita and already played it, I would've still bought it for PC.
Here's hoping that the sequel also gets ported.

Stay away. This game is free but is a complete waste of time. Right off the bat, the game lies to you. You get a launcher and the graphics will say "beautiful" or "fantastic". They are not. They aren't terrible (except out in the street where you don't actually play) but they are nothing special.
The main character talks with the antagonist over the radio. They both swear a lot just because. There is something to be said for having characters talk like real people, but I got the feeling the writer was giggling at how edgy he was being. You get a choice with a branching path but only one is right. If you choose wrong, you go through 2 awful levels and then have to do the other path. You have to avoid an enemy that isn't actually there. If you go toward them, you just die without ever seeing them.
The sound balance is terrible. You have to turn the volume way up to hear the voices but then the rare music or sound effects will blow out your ears.
There is no saving. The levels have names that you have to type in when you select "continue" from the main menu. You can't see what you're typing though. I hope you caught what the level name was when you quit.
Speaking of typing, there is one point where you have to quickly type an answer. There is only one right answer based on one bit of quick dialogue despite the antagonist just before saying "anything" would suffice.
The ONLY thing I can say as a positive is one area called "Park". It actually looks good and has beautiful music.
The game tries to sound like it's playing with a deep philosophical idea, but doesn't deliver, instead just telling you that you had sex with your sister. I'm not kidding. Fail.

Metal Gear Solid V. It's pretty hard to reccomend the game, since what I saw from the trailers and even someone from the studio play it
. In fact, there are many many many things that are mislead during gameplay. There are in fact restrictions, there are limits, and there are certainly some frustrating moments. I will get to those after I peel what is good in the game.
The graphics in the game are absolutly flawless. Very, very well made art and the level design is great. The grass is swaying, and many of the animations are on point. There are things that bugged me though, one of them being that the animations just loop, but it's hard to tell. Another one, and I have been meaning to get to this since the beginning,
. One. That's it. And this just made me so POd when I found out. The side ops are the same damn map the whole way. It does get old after the 2nd side op. Well that's really it for the graphics.
How about the restrictions? Ah, yes. There are indeed restrictions. For example, if you shoot the target, mission is over. If the target dies, mission over. Sure, your helicopter can be blown up, but you get punished for it at the end because it deducts points from you. How is that not a restriction? That really disappointed me when I bought the game expecting not to have any restrictions. Oh yeah, you can't leaave the mission area... or you fail. Yeah, that's not right.
Moving on, the voice acting is incredibly done, as was all of the MG games. Rising, solid, you name it, I think it has really good voice acting. The scripted speeches, you know, the ones where the enemy spots you and radios in, those get repetitive. There are no variations to those lines at all. "This is CP - Understood!" never changes. It's the same guy that says it in the same tone the whole game. No variation at all, and I believe that could have been changed.
Also, the amount of bugs I encountered just by starting the game out was disappointing. I could not use my controller for
reasons. The first one was because the control scheme isn't what it says it is. It says that "Y" is to use but the "DPAD DOWN" button actually uses. The shoot button is right trigger, sure, but aim is "START". Like, that's poor programming right there. Also, I can't really play the game with my controller anyway, since my mouse gets in the game and the camera is forced to be looking up. Can't move or look around at all. So, if you are buying the game for the controller, don't, otherwise you will be so disappointed. Let's move on the the keyboard and mouse controls. I could not get this until I started the game up the 5th time. You can't use a controller. Duh. You know that now. It breaks the game. So being forced to use a keyboard for a console-made game, was not a good concept for me. However, when I tried it, it seemed to integrate flawlessly with keyboard and mouse controls. Even so, it's going to take some getting used to. First off, there are no cover buttons; you have to move up against a wall to take cover, and hold your walk button to get even close to the side of the cover. The dash button says it needs to be held, but the only way to get out of dash mode is to either change stance (crouch) or to tap your walk button, which isn't a bother for me. I made it through the first 15 minutes of figuring out the controls, but I never knew I needed to hold the change stance button to prone. I mean, it's plausable, but still, I think there could've been at least an option maybe to have a prone button? I don't know. Oh well, like I said, you can't just jump in and play on a keyboard; you have to get used to it first. Not so many flaws, but the "ready weapon" while proned is very annoying. If I wanted to lay on my side and start shooting *just* out of my cover, but I need to move a little bit to the right, oh no. There goes my "on the side" technique. Now I am getting shot at from all over. But that's very minor and that's what the actual cover system is for.
Mechanics are a very hard spot of the game; very hard to get perfect, yet easy to bring down the quality of the game. Personally, I have found no problems with the mechanics of the game, besides having the weird menu where you have to use the WASD keys to navigate. Also, if you complete a certain mission, some guy that you rescue is actually ON THE SCREEN in the main menu! I only wanted Snake to be on there! Not this guy no one knows about! Anyway, like I said, no real problems with the mechanics that I could see. You can crawl under buildings and climb over things, you can carry and throw bodies, you can hang off of the only cliff in the game and fall directly into the ocean where it automaticly kills you, etc. Dying isn't really a problem besides the score deduction at the end. It doesn't take too long to get back in the action. The loading screens are actually interactive with hints that you can use the arrow keys to switch hints and read through them. A problem I have found is that it is not very easy to "stick someone up" by holding a gun to their head. I got right behind someone and held a gun to their face, but no, I go into reflex mode and end up shooting the guy. I tried the same thing with at least 5 other soldiers but with the same result. Let's go on to the story.
The story is actually pretty good. There is a backstory, too, since that's what Metal Gear is all about. But one thing that just really, really, REALLY disappoints me, is...
Why? That♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥me off! That was very disappointing, and I would have liked more. There's even a cutscene with Snake in a coma for 9 years. That's a very annoying loose end! How did he get into the coma? Since this isn't revealed in the plot itself, I wouldn't consider this a spoiler. That drove me crazy. I can't comprehend why they would take the story and just take a♥♥♥♥♥♥on it like that. One mission. Really? The rest are side ops. Even the side ops could be tied in with the story! They were so good. "Rescue this guy named, Jarry let's call him, and he has a tape that contains an interrogation between some guy we need to kill and another guy we need to capture" would have been a great objective and might have tied in with the story had it been given some polish. When someone needs to make up a story because a game's side mission could be a part of the story just means that the developers didn't do a very good job with it, and that is bringing down my final score. Speaking of which...
The game is beautiful on the outside, but the devs totally mislead you into buying the game and getting you disappointed. This really♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥me off, but hey, it's still really fun to just sneak around or go in guns blazing and I had a ton of fun playing this game and I still am having fun. That being said, the game is actually pretty good, but not what was expected from the trailers and the dev notes bringing this score to a

Wondership Q is at first glance Terraria with Cats. And it sort of is that. However, it’s got a few tricks up it’s sleeve to really differentiate itself. Which includes Cats. Unfortunately, despite it being a really fun game to play, it’s not something I can really recommend.

With it’s Adorable Aesthetics, a cool and fun ship mechanic, and an interesting premise of providing these sandbox-kind of games with a full plot and direction for the players, Wondership Q is a surprisingly fun time-killer for a few hours. It’s Airship almost acts like a natural extension of the player, and being able to control it separate further compounds that. The game’s adorable characters and well-composed (if generic) aesthetic also really nails a unique level of presentation that makes it very unique. While Wondership Q seems to be dangerously close to being a Terraria Clone, it does have enough tricks on it’s sleeve to give it’s own identity and differentiate itself through it’s more kid-friendly approach to the game.
But what doesn't Wondership Q do right? Unfortunately, quite a lot.
Wondership Q suffers from a lot of poorly executed ideas and a flimsy amount of polish. This is going to be first apparent in the game’s building mechanic. The reticle for placing blocks in this game is determined by the direction you’re facing and the stance you’re in (Crouching, standing). Because of this, building your ship is a freaking nightmare, as you’ll be destroying/removing blocks you didn’t intend to move and before you knew it, you destroyed your entire ship trying to fix some weird mistake on your build. Digging down on certain islands is also a disaster due to being unnecessarily time consuming as you have to deal with the reticle only allowing you to dig paths in mostly 4 different directions. The reticle seems to be designed in mind of say, a Console Game (as such, the game did have a PS4/PS Vita release in Japan under the name Airship Q). But it seems completely strange to me as to why they designed it to be this way, as 2D Crafting/Sandbox games on consoles used something in the vain of Terraria where the Right Stick or some other function would allow you to aim which block you want to destroy or place. Wondership Q only lets you build/destroy in four directions (Left, Right, Lower Left, Lower Right), which is incredibly limiting.
However, to say it’s exactly like a 2D Crafting game like Starbound or Terraria is actually kind of false. Wondership Q takes more in the veins of a 2D RPG with it’s Story Mode, where you go through a handcrafted map activating statues to level up your crafting skills, then craft new items to further progress and collect more statues. Later on, you’ll be tasked with finding four sigils which will be needed to eventually end the game. It’s a interesting premise that ultimately gets bogged down by it slowly becoming more repetitive and exhausting as you play along. Each island in the game doesn’t feel particularly well-designed or takes any use of the game’s strongest mechanics, and thus the entire game devolves into you just thwacking at blocks blocking you from your objective, craft and use a item, get objective, continue progressing. It doesn’t help that the game juggles between being incredibly easy and being a confusing mess. Dying in the game has little to no punishment, Bosses can be defeated in a matter of seconds with either the Sword or a Ship loaded with a ton of cannons, and for the most part the game gives you a generous amount of hitpoints from the get-go. However, it faces issues like a rough English Translation making it difficult to make sense of how items work or what the game wants you to do, and the Physics is incredibly janky and weird to work with, due to it being seemingly unexplained how to make really stable structures in the air.
Wondership Q’s other main deal breaker for some may be how comparatively weak this PC version of the game is. It has no way to modify or change the audio settings (which especially becomes a problem because of the game’s annoying voice acting, sound effects, and generic music), no native video settings or way to make it completely full-screen, and no in-game key mapping (You can manually change it via .ini file). The game could had also really benefited from giving the mouse cursor more use (such as the mouse cursor being the reticle for aiming where to place blocks), as it completely over relies on a finicky Keyboard-only setup that’s uncomfortable no matter how much I try to rearrange it. It also doesn’t include Multiplayer, which was a huge component of the original Airship Q, and it not being here as a local or online method of playing the game with others is surprisingly disappointing, considering it was one of the major selling points of the original game.
Unfortunately, Wondership Q just doesn’t execute and challenge it’s premise very well. It’s main mechanic of a controllable and modifiable ship gets severely underused in the end, and is only mainly used to take down certain bosses or go around as an act of transport. Wondership Q begins as an enjoyable experience, but slowly descends to something that’s repetitive, and often far from challenging the moment the concept of it’s Story Mode starts seeming poorly-designed and unengaging.

Pros

* Easy difficulty (Wish there was harder difficulty options available.)

Note: I imported the Japanese version, Airship Q, and played it that way. I take the PC options into account in my review.
Wondership Q, formerly known as Airship Q, is a Japanese take on the 2D Building/Survival genre. While it has its moments, the game's lack of options and horrible sound effects hold it back from greatness. Its simple gameplay can be fun, but may grow repetitive.
Pros:
Cute graphics.
Airship gameplay is fun.
Story mode is enjoyable.
Cons:
No options, unexcusable for a PC game in 2016.
Horrible sound effects that you cannot turn off.
Gameplay can grow repetitive quickly.
Verdict: Wait for a sale or a patch, because right now it is not worth $10. I would perhaps recommend it at a lower price for fans of the genre, at least as a simple time-waster.

SWISH!  SWISH!  FIGHT!  CRAFTING IS FUN!
So me and my buddy are big fans of Terraria, and Wondership Q caught my attention a few days ago.  I decided to stream it to him this morning as I tried the game out, and almost immediately we rolled in laughter at how basically every action of the cute little protagonist cat is voiced.  It's nonstop, seriously.  I really wish they had displayed this in the videos, because it seems there's no way to turn it off and I'd probably have a much more enjoyable experience after the laughter subsides.
Anyway, the game is as about as cute as you'd expect with some fairly pleasant, simple music.  The building elements seem like they can go pretty far but the game's awkward with a keyboard and with very limited re-mapping, for those of you wondering.  I really like how you can control your ship independently of your character, I was surprised.  There needs to be a fair amount of quality of life improvements though before I'll really invest more time in.
Pros:
Adorable world.
Very smooth animations with nice sprites.
Controlling your ship and character independently offers an interesting gameplay mechanism.
Cons:
Voicework, if only because it just repeats far, far too often with no option to disable.
Very limited re-mapping if you intend to play with a keyboard.
Hard to mine a specific block sometimes; there's not just a range to be able to mine, at least not early on as far as I can tell.  It's only what's directly next to you.
I'm going to recommend it mostly because I think the target audience will enjoy this, and it's fairly priced.  If you're interested at all, watch some videos, know you're going to hear the voicework a -ton-, and if you don't like it there's always Steam's refund policy!  2 hours is more than enough to know if you'll enjoy Wondership Q.

Counter Strike proves, once again, it's core concept is still solid enough to continue on to this very day. While there are plenty of mods around for zombies inside CS 1.6, let alone Source, the game does pitch collectibles, crafting weapons, a neat variety of zombies and bosses, and it overally looks visually appealing and functions well.
However, on the other hand, the crafting system always feels like it's against me, collectible items can sometimes drop in places where you can't get them (though to be fair, the items are locked to a player for a certain time so no item stealing), and weapons you do craft don't last very long without the right materials. The game can get kind of tedious at times, being either too hard to play with basic weapons provided, or too easy with some of the overpowered craftable ones. And even with the super weapons you can craft, some bosses are tedious and generally have the same set-up: boss is big and powerful, hordes attack, do a special thing to avoid an attack. You'll also have to dump a bit of cash to get enough materials to reliably have a good time, though the game is quite generous with points for certain items in the shop.
So...can I recommend it? I guess, tenatively. F2P won't have as much fun unless you kick in a few bucks, and that's up to you if you have the disposible income. Most will probably want to look elsewhere, but it's free, so take a peek. You get a good starter pack, you do get daily rewards and there's nothing to lose from trying.

The whole is even greater than the sum of its parts, and the remake introduced a third faction and an improved translation to the mix.  Highly recommended!
